Getting Started
Configuration
  • Add your API keys in the Integrations/API tab (OpenAI, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, etc.)
  • Create your first agent in Agents page with your preferred LLM, STT, and TTS
  • Configure SIP trunks in Telephony for inbound/outbound calling
Security
  • Enable Two-Factor Authentication in the Security tab
  • Create Sub-Users with limited permissions instead of sharing admin credentials
  • Use HTTPS in production and keep dependencies updated
Tools & Webhooks
  • Assign built-in tools (Hangup, Transfer, SMS) to agents in Tools page
  • Create webhook tools to integrate with n8n, Make.com, or Zapier
Monitoring
  • View live sessions and costs on the Overview page
  • Check Call History for transcriptions and TTFB metrics
  • Monitor services in System Resources tab

 Behind a CDN or load balancer

                    

                    

                        

                            Turn this on only if traffic reaches this dashboard through a
                            service like CloudFront, Cloudflare or a load balancer. Without
                            it, every visitor appears to come from that service instead of
                            their own address — which breaks IP allowlists, makes the
                            audit log show the wrong visitor, and can cause the automatic
                            blocker to ban the service itself, locking out everyone at once.
                        

                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            

                                

                                    
                                    
                                    

                                        Choosing a service fetches its published ranges when you save
                                        and replaces the list below.
                                    

                                

                                

                                    
                                    
                                    

                                        One per line. Only list the ranges belonging to your own
                                        service — anything listed here is allowed to state who
                                        the visitor is.
                                    

                                

                            

                            

                                
                                Your address is currently seen as
                                10.10.10.1.
                                
                                If that is not your own address, the ranges above are not matching yet.
                            

                            

                                
                                After turning this on, check three things.
                                
    
                                    
  • 
                                        IP Lock (Security tab) and any
                                        API key IP allowlists will now be
                                        matched against real visitor addresses instead of
                                        your CDN's. Existing entries listing CDN addresses
                                        will stop matching. Saving here is blocked if it
                                        would lock you out of the dashboard.
                                    
    • 
                                    
  • 
                                        Any existing blocks against your
                                        CDN's own addresses are cleared
                                        automatically when you save, so users
                                        aren't shut out by blocks that were placed for the
                                        wrong reason.
                                    
    • 
                                    
  • 
                                        Automatic blocking keeps working:
                                        because traffic arrives from your CDN, the firewall
                                        can't tell visitors apart, so the dashboard blocks
                                        banned visitors itself instead. Their requests reach
                                        the server before being refused, rather than being
                                        dropped at the network edge.
                                    
    • 
                                

                            

                            
                        


                        


                        
                        
 Block direct access to this server

                        

                            Your server's own address is public and cannot be hidden, so
                            anyone who finds it can skip your CDN and everything it
                            protects you with. Have your CDN add a secret header to every
                            request it sends here, and this dashboard will refuse anything
                            that arrives without it.
                        

                        

                            
                            

                                

                                    
                                    
                                    

                                        Start with Log only for a day. It shows what
                                        would have been refused before anything actually breaks.
                                    

                                

                                

                                    
                                    
                                    
Hyphens only — never underscores.

                                

                                

                                    
                                    

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    
Paste this exact value into your CDN.

                                        did not arrive with the header. Add it to your CDN
                                        and reload this page. Blocking cannot be turned on until this says
                                        it was detected.

  1. Open your distribution → Origins → select your origin → Edit.
    2. 
                                                
  2. Under Add custom header, enter the header name and secret value above.
    3. 
                                                
  3. Save, and wait for the distribution to finish deploying.

    5. 
                                            

                                            
Cloudflare

                                            
    
                                                
  1. Rules → Transform Rules → Modify Request Header.
    2. 
                                                
  2. Create a rule that sets the header name and value above on all requests.
    3.

 Virtual Avatar Providers (Chatbot Agents)

                    

                        
                        Avatar providers add a lip-synced talking-head video to chatbot agents.
                        Each provider runs in their own cloud and joins the LiveKit room as a separate participant —
                        your dashboard must be reachable from the public internet for the avatar provider to connect inbound.
                        Configure these per-chatbot under the Avatar tab in each chatbot agent's editor.
                    

                    

                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            Realistic photo-based avatars. Requires a v4 expressive avatar created in D-ID Studio.
                            
                        


                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            Hyper-realistic video avatars. Requires a Replica ID + a Persona configured for LiveKit transport.
                            
                        


                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            Fastest setup — works with Beyond Presence's stock avatar by default. Optional custom Avatar ID.
                            
                        


                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            LiveAvatar-powered avatars. Generate the key at app.liveavatar.com/developers (NOT HeyGen's main site — they are separate). Avatar ID is required and chosen on the chatbot's Avatar tab. Click Test to also see how many concurrent sessions are currently active on your account (free tier limit = 1).
                            
                        

                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            Lifelike low-latency avatars. Generate the key at lab.anam.ai/api-keys. Pick a stock Avatar ID from the Avatar Gallery or build a custom avatar in Anam Lab, then paste the ID on the chatbot's Avatar tab.
                            
                        

                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            Low-latency real-time faces (Trinity model). Generate the key at app.simli.com/apikey. Pick a Face ID from the default library or upload your own, then paste it on the chatbot's Avatar tab. Free tier: 50 min/month. Priced per minute on Settings → Pricing → Avatar Providers.
                            
                        

                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            Realtime avatars up to 1280×720 with optional custom backgrounds. Generate the key in the Avatario dashboard and copy a stock Avatar ID from the same dashboard, then paste it on the chatbot's Avatar tab. No Test button: Avatario has no read-only endpoint (its only call starts a billable session) — verify by starting a chatbot session. Avatario publishes no price: set your rate on Settings → Pricing → Avatar Providers.

Each chatbot generates its own webhook URL — paste that into your provider's console. WhatsApp is available through Sent.dm — one number covers both channels.

Twilio uses HMAC-SHA1 webhook signatures (verified automatically).

                        About Vertex AI latency:
                        Vertex has inherent overhead (service-account OAuth, GCP project routing) that makes it ~100–300ms slower per turn than Google AI Studio for voice agents. If raw speed matters more than enterprise compliance (IAM / audit / data residency), prefer the google provider (AI Studio) on your agents, or enable the Priority Tier toggle below (~2× cost).

 AWS (Bedrock LLM & Transcribe STT)

                    

                        
                        AWS Services: These credentials are used for Bedrock LLM (Claude, Amazon Nova), Transcribe STT, and Nova Sonic Realtime.
                        They are separate from S3 storage credentials below.
                        


                         Regional models: Models marked as "(Regional)" in the agent editor will automatically use the appropriate inference profile based on the AWS Region you select below.
                        


                         IAM Permissions: For Transcribe STT, ensure your IAM user has transcribe:StartStreamTranscription and transcribe:StartStreamTranscriptionWebSocket permissions.
                    


                    
                    
 Geo-Located Models (AWS Bedrock)

                    

                        
                        AWS Bedrock: Regionally hosted AI models for low-latency, geo-located inference. Models are hosted in your selected AWS region for optimal performance and data residency.
                    

                    

                        

                             Cross-Region Inference Profiles
                        

                        

                            
AWS Bedrock uses cross-region inference profiles to route requests to the optimal region. There are two types of models available:

                            

                                
                                    

                                        Model Type
                                        Prefix
                                        Behavior
                                    

                                
                                
                                    

                                        APAC Models
(e.g., Claude Sonnet 4, Haiku 3)		
                                        apac.
                                        Routes to any Asia-Pacific region for load balancing. Good for older models.
                                    

                                    

                                        Regional Models
(e.g., Claude Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5)		
                                        au. / jp. / us. / eu.
                                        Routes within a specific geographic area based on your AWS Region setting. Required for Claude 4.5 models.
                                    

                                
                            

                            

                                 Note: Claude Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 are not available via the apac. prefix.
                                Use the "(Regional)" models which automatically select the correct prefix based on your configured AWS Region
                                (e.g., ap-southeast-2 → au., ap-northeast-1 → jp.).

                            Your AWS secret access key.
                        


                        

                            
                            
                            Primary AWS region for Bedrock LLM & Transcribe STT. Cross-region inference profiles (APAC, AU, Global) route automatically regardless of this setting.
                        

                    


                    

                        

                            
                            
                            Region for Nova Sonic realtime. Falls back to AWS Region above if not set.
                        

                        

                            
                            
                            Region for Amazon Polly TTS. Generative engine requires us-east-1 or us-west-2.
                        

                    


                    

                        

                            
                            
                            

                                Adds the serviceTier parameter to every Bedrock text-LLM call (voice agents, text-mode agents, and web chat).
                                Applies globally to all Bedrock models. Not supported on Nova Sonic realtime — realtime always uses Standard.
                                AWS supports tiers on a per-model basis: models that support the selected tier get it automatically, and models that
                                don’t simply run on Standard (verified per model in the background — calls never fail because of this setting).
                                
                                    Learn more 
                                
                            

                            
                        

                    


                    

                    

                    
 Azure (Microsoft) — LLM / STT / TTS / Realtime

                    

                        
                        Azure OpenAI & Azure AI Foundry: Hosts OpenAI's GPT family, Microsoft's Phi-4, xAI's Grok, Mistral, and Meta's Llama — all reachable through the same OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API via deployment names.
                        
Get credentials from Azure Portal > your OpenAI resource > Keys and Endpoint.
                        
How the sections work: the Azure LLM section is the master Azure OpenAI resource. The Whisper (STT), OpenAI (TTS) and Realtime options inherit the LLM section's endpoint / key / API version when their fields are left blank; only fill them to point a service at a different Azure OpenAI resource — most useful for Realtime, which Azure serves only in East US 2 / Sweden Central. The Azure Speech neural voices (incl. en-AU) use their own Region + Speech Key in each section.
                        
Endpoint format: use your Azure OpenAI Service endpoint (*.openai.azure.com). Azure AI Foundry MaaS endpoints (*.services.ai.azure.com) follow a different URL pattern and won't work — deploy Foundry models inside an Azure OpenAI resource instead.

 Chatbot API

                

                    
Lets your own software use a chatbot without the website widget (start a chat, send a message and get the reply straight back, read the transcript, end the chat) and send a text message from a chatbot’s SMS number. Same keys as above; both switches are off until you turn them on. API chats show up in Chat History like web chats, with their cost. The REST API switch above must also be on.

                    

                        

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            /external/v1/chats
                        

                        

                            
                            
                            0 = unlimited. Messages are capped at 10× this.
                        

                        

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            /external/v1/sms
                        

                        

                            
                            
                            0 = unlimited. The chatbot’s own SMS daily cap applies per destination.
                        

                    

                    

                        Good to know: API chats have no memory across chats (like SMS); the sender of an API SMS is always the chatbot’s configured number; a chat nobody ends is closed after the chatbot’s inactivity timeout; any key with “Can Make Calls” can use every enabled chatbot — treat keys as passwords. Details and examples are in the User Guide (Chatbot Agents → REST API).
                    

                

            


            
            

                

                    
 API Keys

                    
                

                

                    
                    

                        
                        
No REST API keys configured. Generate a key to enable external call triggering.

                    

                    
                

            


            
            

                

                    
 Example: Trigger a Call

                    
                

                

                    
Send a POST request with a Bearer token to trigger an outbound call. In n8n, paste the Bearer token into an HTTP Request node.

                    
curl -X POST https://vaai.aetosiot.com/external/v1/calls \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-rest-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "agent_slug": "your-agent-slug",
    "to_number": "+61400000000",
    "from_number": "+61388430777",
    "dynamic_variables": {
      "Name": "Jane Doe",
      "CompanyName": "Acme Corp"
    }
  }'

                    Dynamic variables are substituted into {{Name}}-style placeholders in the agent's system prompt and greeting at call time.

 MCP Server — User Guide

                    
                

                


                    
 What is the MCP Server?

                    
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard language that AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor speak. Enabling the MCP Server lets those AI tools connect directly to this dashboard — so you can ask your AI assistant to list your agents, look up recent calls, check analytics, or even create and update agents, all without opening the browser UI.

                    
Think of it as giving your AI assistant a secure, controlled set of keys to your dashboard.


                    

                    
 What can an AI assistant do through MCP?

                    
    
                        
  • List, create, update, and delete agents
    • 
                        
  • Query call history and pull analytics
    • 
                        
  • Manage SIP trunks and inbound dispatch rules
    • 
                        
  • Check system health and service status
    • 
                        
  • Manage the knowledge base and agent tools
    • 
                        
  • Run campaign outbound dial jobs
    • 
                    

                    
The full list of available actions is shown in the "Claude Code Configuration" card on this same page.


                    

                    
 Setup — Step by Step

                    
    
                        
  1. Enable the MCP Server — Use the toggle at the top of the MCP Server Status card on this page. The status dot will turn green when it is running.
    2. 
                        
  2. Generate a key — Click Generate New Key in the API Keys section. Give the key a descriptive name (e.g., "Claude Code – My Laptop").
    3. 
                        
  3. Choose a permission level:
                            
      
                                
    • Read Only — The AI assistant can view agents, calls, and analytics, but cannot make any changes.
      • 
                                
    • Read & Write — Full access: the AI can create and update agents, trigger calls, etc.
      • 
                            
    
                        
    4. 
                        
  4. Add an IP allowlist — Enter the IP address of the computer where your AI assistant runs (e.g., your laptop's IP). This stops anyone else from using the key even if it leaks. Leave blank only if you are comfortable with no IP restriction.
                            
    Example: 203.0.113.42
                        
    5. 
                        
  5. Copy the key — The key (starting with sk-mcp-) is shown once immediately after you click Generate. Copy it now — it cannot be retrieved later.
    6. 
                        
  6. Configure your AI assistant — In Claude Code, paste the JSON configuration block shown in the "Claude Code Configuration" card on this page into your MCP settings file. Replace the sk-mcp-… placeholder with the key you just copied.
    7. 
                    


                    

                    
 MCP vs REST API — What's the difference?

                    
These are two separate systems with separate keys:

                    
    
                        
  • MCP Server — For AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor). Keys start with sk-mcp-.
    • 
                        
  • REST API — For workflow tools (n8n, Zapier, Make). Keys start with sk-rest-.
    • 
                    

                    
An MCP key will not work on the REST API, and vice versa.


                    

                    
 Keeping Your Key Safe

                    
    
                        
  • Never share your key or commit it to a code repository.
    • 
                        
  • Use the IP allowlist to restrict access to your machine only.
    • 
                        
  • If a key is ever leaked, delete it immediately from the API Keys list and generate a fresh one.
    • 
                    


                    

                    
 Troubleshooting

                    
    
                        
  • 401 Unauthorized — The key is wrong, expired, or the MCP Server toggle is off. Check both.
    • 
                        
  • 403 Forbidden — Your key is Read Only but the AI tried to make a change. Generate a Read & Write key instead.
    • 
                        
  • 429 Too Many Requests — Rate limit reached (default: 60 requests per minute per key). Wait a moment and try again.
    •

 REST API — User Guide

                    
                

                


                    
 What is the REST API?

                    
The REST API lets external tools — like n8n, Zapier, or Make — trigger outbound calls automatically when something happens in another system. For example: a new lead fills in a form → n8n fires an HTTP request → the dashboard calls the lead using your AI agent.

                    
No coding required on your end — you just build a simple workflow in your automation tool.


                    

                    
 Setup — Step by Step

                    
    
                        
  1. Enable the REST API Server — Use the toggle on the REST API Server Status card on this page. The status dot turns green when it is running.
    2. 
                        
  2. Generate a key — Click Generate New Key in the REST API Keys section below. Give it a name like "n8n – Production".
    3. 
                        
  3. Choose a permission level:
                            
      
                                
    • Can Make Calls — Lets the workflow trigger outbound calls AND look up call status.
      • 
                                
    • Read Only — Only allows looking up call status; cannot trigger new calls.
      • 
                            
    
                        
    4. 
                        
  4. Add an IP allowlist — Enter the IP address of your n8n server (or other tool's server). This ensures only that server can use the key.
                            
    Example: 203.0.113.10
                        
    5. 
                        
  5. Copy the key — The key (starting with sk-rest-) is shown once right after you click Generate. Copy it now — you cannot retrieve it later.
    6. 
                        
  6. In n8n (or similar tool), create an HTTP Request node with these settings:
                            
      
                                
    • Method: POST
      • 
                                
    • URL: https://your-dashboard-address/external/v1/calls
      • 
                                
    • Header: Authorization: Bearer sk-rest-…
      • 
                                
    • Body (JSON): see the example below
      • 
                            
    
                        
    7. 
                    


                    

                    
 Example Request Body

                    
{
  "agent_slug": "sales-follow-up",
  "to_number": "+61412345678",
  "from_number": "+61398765432",
  "dynamic_variables": {
    "Name": "Jane",
    "CompanyName": "Acme Corp"
  }
}

                    
Replace sales-follow-up with your agent's slug (shown in the agent list). to_number is the number to call; from_number is your SIP trunk number.


                    

                    
 Dynamic Variables — Personalising the Call

                    
Any keys you send in dynamic_variables are automatically inserted into your agent's system prompt wherever you have placed a matching placeholder. Placeholders look like this: {{Name}}.

                    
Example: Your agent's prompt contains "Hi {{Name}} from {{CompanyName}}, I'm calling about…". You send {"Name": "Jane", "CompanyName": "Acme"}. The agent will say "Hi Jane from Acme, I'm calling about…"


                    

                    
 Available Endpoints

                    
    
                        
  • POST /external/v1/calls — Trigger a new outbound call. Requires "Can Make Calls" permission.
    • 
                        
  • GET /external/v1/calls/{call_id} — Look up the status of a call by its ID. Works with both permission levels.
    • 
                    


                    

                    
 Keeping Your Key Safe

                    
    
                        
  • Never paste your key into a public place or commit it to a code repository.
    • 
                        
  • Use the IP allowlist to limit access to your automation server only.
    • 
                        
  • If a key is ever leaked, delete it from the REST API Keys list immediately and generate a new one.
    • 
                    


                    

                    
 Troubleshooting

                    
    
                        
  • 401 Unauthorized — The key is wrong or the REST API Server toggle is off. Check both.
    • 
                        
  • 403 Forbidden — Your key is Read Only but the workflow tried to trigger a call. Generate a "Can Make Calls" key instead.
    • 
                        
  • 400 Bad Request — A required field is missing from your request body (usually agent_slug, to_number, or from_number).
    • 
                        
  • 404 Not Found — The agent_slug doesn't match any agent in the dashboard. Check the exact slug in your agent list.
    • 
                        
  • 503 Service Unavailable — The REST API Server is toggled off. Enable it on this page.
    •

                    Check Compatibility Before Upgrading!
                    

                        Always verify that new package versions are compatible with your other dependencies before upgrading.
                        Some packages (like boto3, aiobotocore, and LiveKit plugins) have strict version constraints.
                        Upgrading to the latest version without checking can cause dependency conflicts and break your installation.

 Swap Memory

                
            

            

                
Swap provides virtual memory when physical RAM is full. Swappiness controls how aggressively the system uses swap.


                

                    

                        Loading...
                    

                    Loading swap info...
                


                
                

                    

                        

                            
 No Swap Detected

                            
This server has no swap memory configured. Swap acts as a safety net when physical RAM runs out, preventing out-of-memory crashes.

 Recommended Swap Settings for LiveKit


                            
                            

                                

                                    0-10: Minimal swap

                                    Only use when RAM is critical. Best for systems with plenty of RAM.
                                

                                

                                    30-60: Balanced (Default)

                                    Good for most workloads. 60 is the Linux default.
                                

                                

                                    80-100: Aggressive swap

                                    Use swap more freely. May help on very low RAM systems.
                                

                            


                            


                            
                            

                                

                                    
Why RAM is preferred over Swap:

                                    
    
                                        
  • Latency: RAM operates at nanosecond speeds; swap uses disk I/O (milliseconds), causing audio/video delays
    • 
                                        
  • Real-time processing: STT, TTS, and LLM inference require instant memory access for smooth call quality
    • 
                                        
  • Consistency: Swap causes unpredictable pauses when pages are loaded from disk mid-call
    • 
                                    

                                

                                

                                    
Recommended Settings:

                                    
    
                                        
  • Swappiness: 10 (only use swap as last resort)
    • 
                                        
  • Swap Size: 1-2GB minimum (safety net for memory spikes)
    • 
                                        
  • Best Practice: Provision adequate RAM rather than relying on swap
    • 
                                        
  • Monitoring: If swap usage is consistently high, add more RAM
    •

 Monthly Invoicing

        

        

          

            
            
          

          

            Emails each of your customers a monthly invoice for the calls made by
            the agents assigned to them, at your marked-up prices. While this is
            off nothing is collected and nothing is sent.
          

        

      


      
      

        

          
 Your business

        

        

          

            

              
              
              
Printed as the issuer on every invoice.

            

            

              
              
              
Where your customers reply about an invoice.

            

            

              
              
            

            

              
              
            

            

              
              
              
ABN, VAT No., GST No., EIN — whatever your country uses.

            

            

              
              
            

          

        

      


      
      

        

          
 Tax

        

        

          

            
            
          

          

            

              
              
            

            

              
              
            

            

              
              
            

          

          

            
            One tax rate applies to every customer. Cross-border treatment —
            reverse charge, a customer's own tax number on the face, statutory
            wording — is not supported, so use this for domestic invoicing only.
          

        

      


      
      

        

          
 Invoice numbers

        

        

          

            

              
              
            

            

              
              
              
Must differ from the invoice prefix.

            

            

              
              
              

                
                  One continuous sequence across all customers.
                
              

            

          

        

      


      
      

        

          
 Payment

        

        

          

            

              
              
              
The due date is the invoice date plus this many days.

            

            

              
              
            

            

              
              
              
Printed on every invoice. Free text, so any country's format works.

            

          

        

      


      
      

        

          
 Presentation

        

        

          

            

              
              
              
Costs are recorded in USD and converted at the rate on the Pricing tab.

            

            

              
              
            

          

        

      


      

        
      

    


  


  
  

    

      

        
 Readiness

      

      

        
        

           Invoices cannot be issued yet.
          
    
            
  • No business name is set — an invoice must name its issuer.
    • 
          

        

        

        
    
          
          
  • 
            
              
            
            Business name
            
              Blocks invoicing
            
            
    Printed as the issuer on every invoice
    
          
    • 
          
          
  • 
            
              
            
            Business address
            
            
    Most jurisdictions require it on a tax invoice
    
          
    • 
          
          
  • 
            
              
            
            Invoice currency
            
            
    USD to AUD @ 1.58 — built-in default, confirm it on the Pricing tab
    
          
    • 
          
          
  • 
            
              
            
            Tax configuration
            
            
    No tax line on invoices
    
          
    • 
          
          
  • 
            
              
            
            Payment details
            
            
    How the customer pays you — bank details, payment link
    
          
    • 
          
          
  • 
            
              
            
            Email delivery
            
            
    Invoices are delivered by email — configure the Email tab
    
          
    • 
          
        

      

    


    

      

        
 How it works

      

      

        
Each of your customers is a user on the Users tab with a margin
        percentage. They are invoiced for the calls made by the agents assigned
        to them, priced at your cost plus their margin.

        
An invoice is a fixed record once issued: changing your
        prices, tax rate, an agent's name or even the dashboard timezone
        afterwards never alters an invoice that has already been sent.

      

    

  



                    

                        




  

    
 Preview a period

  

  

    

      See exactly what would be invoiced, and what would be blocked and why,
      before anything is sent. This only looks — it issues no invoice
      number, sends no email, and changes nothing.
    

    

      

        
      

      
        
        Adding up the month…

          This is a preview. The invoice number is allocated when it is
          actually issued, so it shows as PREVIEW here.

 Template Variables Reference

                    

                    

                        

                            Use these variables in your email templates. Variables use the {{variable}} syntax.
                            For conditional content, use {{#variable}}content{{/variable}}.
                        

                        

                            

                                
Common Variables

                                

                                    
                                        

                                            {{from_name}}
                                            Sender display name (from Email Settings)
                                        

                                        

                                            {{from_email}}
                                            Sender email address
                                        

                                        

                                            {{logo_url}}
                                            URL to custom logo (if configured)
                                        

                                        

                                            {{dashboard_link}}
                                            Link to relevant dashboard page
                                        

                                        

                                            {{timestamp}}
                                            Current date/time when email is sent
                                        

                                    
                                

                            

                            

                                
Password Reset Variables

                                

                                    
                                        

                                            {{username}}
                                            User's name or email
                                        

                                        

                                            {{reset_link}}
                                            Password reset URL
                                        

                                    
                                

                                
Conditional Example

                                {{#logo_url}}<img src="{{logo_url}}">{{/logo_url}}
                                
Shows logo only if custom logo is configured

                     Call & Chat History Storage
                

            

            

                

                    
                    These settings control where call and chat session metadata (summaries, transcriptions, call details) are stored.
                


                
                
 Storage Provider

                

                    

                    

                        
                        

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            

                                
                                
                            

                        

                        Configure cloud storage credentials in the Integrations/API tab
                    


                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            Australia/Sydney
                        

                        When this section's daily deletion run happens, in the time zone set in Settings → Time & Date. Applies to this section's retention rules. Nothing is deleted while retention is “Keep forever”.
                    


                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                days after the call
                            

                        

                        Voice call records and transcripts stored on this server. Kept forever by default. Chatbot & SMS history has its own rule in the Chat History section below.
                    


                    
                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                days after the archive date
                            

                        

                        Voice call records archived in your bucket. Kept forever by default — setting a period permanently deletes older archives from your bucket (whole-day granularity, so the boundary can differ from the local rule by up to a day). Backups and diagnostics data are never touched.
                    

                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                

                

                


                
                

                    

                        
 Cloud Sync

                        Copy call & chat history between Redis and cloud storage.
                    

                    

                        

                            
                            
                            
                            
                        

                    

                


                
                


                


                
                
 AI Summary Settings

                

                    

                        

                            
                            
                        

                        Automatically generate AI summaries when calls complete
                        

                            
                            
                        

                        Hide the Regenerate / model-selection controls on each call's Summary tab (makes summaries view-only)
                        

                            
                            
                        

                        After each voice call's summary, run LiveKit's evaluation judges on the transcript (safety, relevancy, task completion…). Verdicts show on the call page and feed AutoResearch's problem-call list. Needs Auto-generate on; uses the same provider/model; roughly one summary's worth of tokens per judge per call (the summary Max Tokens setting does not cap judges).
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            
                            

                                
                                
                            

                            
                        

                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                


                
                
                

                    
                         Advanced Summary Settings
                    
                    

                        

                            

                                

                                    
                                    
                                

                                
                                Instructions prepended to every summary request. Controls language, format, and analysis focus.
                            

                            

                                

                                    
                                    
                                

                                
                                Defines the AI's role and behavior. Controls accuracy, tone, and output format rules.
                            

                            

                                

                                    
                                    
                                    Maximum response length. Increase for long calls (500–8000).
                                

                                

                                    
                                    
                                    Lower = more consistent, higher = more creative (0–1).
                                

                            

                        

                    

                

                

                

                     Configure API keys in the Integrations/API tab to enable AI summaries.
                


                


                
                
 Minimum Duration Filter

                

                    

                    

                        

                            
                            
                        

                        When enabled, calls shorter than the specified duration will not be added to call or chat history.
                    

                    

                        
                        
                        1-300 seconds
                    

                    

                        
                    

                

            

        


        
        

        
        

            

                

                     Chat History
                

            

            

                

                    One rule for everything on the chat page: chatbot conversation records & transcripts,
                    website widget messages, and SMS conversations. Widget messages and SMS always live on this
                    server (they are never sent to cloud storage), so the "on this server" rule always applies to them.
                    Chat history lives in server memory (Redis) — keeping everything forever grows memory use over time on busy widgets.
                

                

                    

                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            Australia/Sydney
                        

                        When this section's daily deletion run happens, in the time zone set in Settings → Time & Date. Note: widget and SMS messages are exact-expiry — they are removed exactly N days after the last message regardless of this time; this time controls when chatbot conversation records are cleaned up. Nothing is deleted while retention is “Keep forever”.
                    


                    

                        
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                days after the last message
                            

                        

                        Sliding rule: a conversation is removed this many days after its latest message (calls use a fixed "days after the call" rule instead). Applies to chatbot conversations, widget messages and SMS threads together.
                    


                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                days after the archive date
                            

                        

                        Chatbot conversation records archived in your bucket (used when call & chat history storage is S3/GCS). Setting a period permanently deletes older archives from your bucket. Backups and diagnostics data are never touched.
                    

                    

                    

                        
                        

                            
                            messages
                        

                        Blank = keep every message (default). If set, each widget/SMS conversation keeps only its newest messages — trimming is irreversible.
                    


                    

                        
                    

                

                
            

        


        
        

            

                

                     Recording Storage
                

            

            

                

                    
                    These settings control where call recordings (audio files) are stored.
                


                
                
 Recording Destination & Format

                

                    

                    

                        
                        

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            

                                
                                
                            

                        

                        Configure cloud storage credentials in the Integrations/API tab
                    


                    
                    

                        

                            
                            
                        

                    


                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            Australia/Sydney
                        

                        When this section's daily deletion run happens, in the time zone set in Settings → Time & Date. Applies to this section's retention rules. Nothing is deleted while retention is “Keep forever”.
                    


                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                days after the recording was made
                            

                        

                        Keep forever means audio files are never removed from this server's disk — recordings are the biggest storage users, so watch the disk usage above. Applies whichever storage location is selected (local copies can also exist with cloud storage when "Delete local after cloud upload" is off).
                    


                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                days after the archive date
                            

                        

                        Setting a period permanently deletes older audio files from your bucket. Backups and diagnostics data are never touched.
                    

                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                


                


                
                
 Minimum Duration Filter

                

                    

                    

                        

                            
                            
                        

                        When enabled, recordings shorter than the specified duration will be automatically deleted when calls end.
                    

                    

                        
                        
                        1-300 seconds
                    

                    

                        
                    

                

            

        


        
        
        

            

                

                     Observability Storage
                

            

            

                

                    
                    Where event timelines, OpenTelemetry traces, and correlated logs are archived after each call. Hot-tier data lives in Redis; the gzipped cold-tier blobs land here.
                


                
 Storage Provider

                

                    

                    

                        
                        

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            

                                
                                
                            

                            

                                
                                
                            

                        

                        Each cold-tier blob is gzipped (~5–30 KB per call). Configure cloud credentials in Recording Storage above; observability shares them.
                    


                    

                        
 Retention — each tier has its own window

                        

                            

                                
                                

                                    
                                    days
                                

                                Recent calls open instantly from memory. Older calls load from the archive with a small delay — nothing is lost.
                            

                            

                                
                                

                                    
                                    MB
                                

                                Hard cap on Redis memory used by observability. If call volume grows, the oldest archived calls are evicted first.
                            

                            

                                
                                

                                    
                                    days
                                

                                Window for the on-disk copies. Not applicable when "skip local fallback" is ticked. With no cloud storage, this IS the archive window.
                            

                            

                                
                                

                                    
                                    days
                                

                                The long archive window on S3/GCS. After this, the call's observability is deleted everywhere.
                            

                        

                        

                            

                                
                                

                                    
                                    % of disk
                                

                                Local-only safety cap. Cloud bucket size is controlled by the cloud retention setting (and any S3/GCS lifecycle rules you configure on the bucket).
                            

                            

                                
                                

                                    
                                    
                                

                                Total size of the archived blobs — local files plus the cloud bucket's observability/ folder.
                            

                            

                                
                                

                                    
                                    of 256 MB
                                

                                Live memory used by recent calls in Redis, against the size limit above.
                            

                        

                    


                    
                    

                        

                            
                            
                        

                        
                            On by default when cloud storage is configured — the archive lives in S3/GCS only and nothing is written to local disk. Untick to also keep a small (~30 KB/call) gzipped local copy of every bundle, which gives disaster recovery if cloud access is ever lost and slightly faster reads of archived calls.
                        
                    


                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                


                
 Prompts in traces

                
                

                    Each LLM turn's trace can keep the full system prompt, the conversation so far and the
                    tool definitions that were sent. That is useful for prompt debugging, but it contains
                    everything the caller said and makes each call's diagnostic bundle much larger.
                

                

                    
                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                    

                


                
            

        


        
        
        

            

                

                     Call Audio Processing
                

            

            

                
                

                    
                    How the server processes the caller's voice during calls. Phone lines carry
                    narrow-band audio, so 16 kHz processing lowers CPU per call with no audible
                    difference on phone calls. Changes apply from the next call — no restart needed.
                

                

                    
                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                    

                


                

                
                
 Caller volume levelling (noise-cancelled calls)

                
                

                    When an agent uses noise cancellation, the server can also level the caller's volume
                    (automatic gain control) before the agent hears it. In our tests it made no measurable
                    difference to speech recognition or turn detection, so either choice is safe;
                    On is how every call has run so far.
                

                

                    
                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                    

                

            

        


        
        
        

            

                

                     Call Recording Audio
                

            

            

                

                    
                    How call recordings are made. Both settings apply to new recordings
                    only — each recording keeps the layout and quality it was made with, and you can
                    switch back at any time. Changes apply from the next call — no restart needed.
                

                

                    
                    

                        

                            
                            
                            
                                OGG is ~50% smaller than MP4 for voice calls, and the quality tiers'
                                full size savings apply only to OGG.
                            
                        

                        

                            
                            
                            
                                Dual Channel makes transcription diagnostics and speaker separation far
                                more accurate. On headphones each party plays in one ear (a single earbud
                                plays only one party). Requires a recent recording component — older
                                installs simply keep recording mixed.
                            
                        

                        

                            
                            
                            
                                Size savings apply fully with the OGG recording format (Recording Storage
                                above); MP4 recordings currently shrink only slightly — a limitation of the
                                recording component. Quality can't be undone for recordings already made,
                                and lower tiers reduce Improvement Lab replay fidelity (with Dual Channel
                                on, each party gets half the tier's bitrate). New installs start with
                                OGG + Dual Channel + Efficient; installs upgraded from earlier versions keep
                                their existing settings until changed here.
                            
                        

                    

                    

                        
                    

                

            

        

    

    
        

        
    


    

            

                

                    
 Community Edition Licensing

                    
This dashboard is running the Community Edition — a free tier of the full product.
                       Everything works exactly like the full version, with one limit:

                    
    
                        
  • Voice Agents: up to 2 voice agents can exist on this install.
    • 
                        
  • Chatbot Agents: up to 2 chatbot agents can exist on this install.
    • 
                    


                    
How the limit behaves

                    
    
                        
  • Existing agents keep working: if this install already has more agents than the limit,
                            none of them are disabled — they all keep taking calls and chats as normal.
    • 
                        
  • Creating new agents: the Create, Templates, Duplicate and Import options are blocked
                            while the install is at or above the limit. Deleting an agent only frees a slot once you are
                            below the limit.
    • 
                        
  • API access: the MCP API's agent-creation tools follow the same limit.
    • 
                    


                    
Upgrading to a full licence

                    
A full licence removes the agent limits entirely — unlimited voice agents and chatbots, with no other changes
                       to your setup, agents, or data.

                    
    
                        
  • Join the community: LiveKit Dashboard Skool community
    • 
                        
  • Contact: email voiceai@tronic.com.au to organise your upgrade.
    • 
                    


                    

                        After you upgrade: the limits lift automatically on the next successful licence check.
                        Checks run on their own every day or two — or apply it immediately via
                        Settings → Updates → Check for Updates. No reinstall and no restart needed;
                        the Community Edition badge and this tab disappear within about a minute of the check.
