 Release Notes

                    

                    

                        
                        

                            

                                v1.39.0 Latest
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Human Handoff: a website or SMS conversation can now be passed to a real person. Visitors get a “Talk to a person” button, your team is notified through your own workflow tool, and their replies appear in the chat as if they were typing in it. The agent steps back while a person is on, and picks up again afterwards. Everything the person says is kept in the conversation transcript.
    • 
                                
  • Answering machine detection on outbound calls: a new detection method that recognises voicemail far more reliably than before, and knows the difference between a person saying hello and a recorded greeting. It waits out long voicemail messages instead of giving up early. New agents use it by default; existing agents keep the method they already had until you change it.
    • 
                                
  • Theme & Appearance: recolour the whole dashboard, login page included. Choose a colour preset or your own accent colour, a background tone, a text colour and a system font. The main administrator also gets a Custom CSS box for finer control. If a style ever hides something, add ?safe_theme=1 to the address to load the page without it and press Reset.
    • 
                                
  • Website chat gets the full voice control set: chatbot agents now offer the same speech recognition, voice, conversation dynamics and recording options as phone agents, arranged in the same sub-tabs. Many more speech providers are now selectable on chatbots.
    • 
                                
  • Record website voice chats: full-voice widget sessions can be recorded like phone calls. By default the visitor is asked first and nothing is recorded until they agree. Recordings appear on the chat’s page in Chat History and on the Recording page. Please check what notice or consent your state or country requires before turning this on.
    • 
                                
  • Copy an agent between phone and website: turn a voice agent into a chatbot, or a chatbot into a voice agent, in one step. Shared settings, tools and knowledge bases come across; anything that only makes sense on the other channel is left behind, and you see exactly what will happen before you confirm.
    • 
                                
  • Orb Style for the chat widget: the voice orb has three looks — Classic, Circle and Bars. Circle and Bars react to the caller’s and the agent’s voice in your own brand colour, and are used both for the large orb and the small indicator inside the chat. New chatbots start on Circle; existing ones keep the look they have.
    • 
                                
  • Chat and SMS API: an optional interface for sending your own conversations and text messages through an agent from another system. Off by default, with its own per-key limits.
    • 
                                
  • Noise Cancellation Lab: a new tab in the Improvement Lab that replays real calls through different noise-cancellation settings and ranks the results side by side.
    • 
                                
  • Simulation improvements: tests can now assert that an agent actually used the right tool, and call-quality judges can score real calls automatically.
    • 
                                
  • Two more avatar providers: Simli and Avatario join the existing avatar options, and every avatar service is now priced per minute so avatar time shows on the call cost.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Updated voice engine: the LiveKit Agents 1.8.0 runtime family, with the caller microphone levelling now under your control and reasoning token usage shown on the Call Detail page.
    • 
                                
  • New models and voices: AssemblyAI Universal-3.6 Pro, Gemini 3.8 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash, Fish Audio S2.1 Pro, extra Deepgram Flux transcript options (numbers, profanity filtering, redaction) and secondary languages for ElevenLabs Scribe.
    • 
                                
  • Text-only chatbots no longer need speech keys: a text chatbot starts without Deepgram or Cartesia credentials, and one voice agent missing a key no longer stops the whole agent service from starting.
    • 
                                
  • Sub-user permissions: a thorough review of who can reach what. Pages that only checked whether you were logged in now check your actual permissions, and administrator-only areas such as updates, restarts and security settings are properly restricted.
    • 
                                
  • Delete conversations: Chat History can now delete website and SMS conversations, with the recording removed alongside them.
    • 
                                
  • New installs start leaner: a brand new dashboard now defaults to the efficient recording format and audio settings. Existing installs are left exactly as they are.
    • 
                                
  • User Guide: substantially expanded, with fresh screenshots throughout and phone numbers masked.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Telnyx voices: Telnyx retired its NaturalHD voices, which left affected agents silent. Agents using them are moved automatically to a working voice.
    • 
                                
  • Groq models: Groq retired its Llama chat models; agents pointing at them now resolve to a working model instead of failing.
    • 
                                
  • Answering machine detection: the maximum wait now allows for ringing and for long voicemail greetings, instead of cutting the check short.
    • 
                                
  • Sub-user sign-in: fixed redirect loops for staff accounts without an Overview page or with a disabled account, and the Edit User form now always acts on the account you opened.
    • 
                                
  • Chatbot editor: the Preview Widget button is now clearly visible, the widget preview matches what the widget actually looks like, and settings that do not apply to the chosen display mode explain themselves instead of appearing broken.
    • 
                                
  • Speech recognition: Telnyx transcription no longer stops after the first result.
    • 
                            

                        

                        
                        

                            

                                v1.38.1
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Silence check-ins now repeat: when a caller goes quiet, the agent re-engages at your configured interval until the “max re-engagement attempts” limit is reached, then says a polite goodbye and ends the call cleanly. Previously only one check-in was ever spoken and the call sat in dead air until the hard silence timeout.
    • 
                                
  • Per-agent silence settings on handoffs: after a transfer or transition, the agent currently handling the call now uses its own silence re-engagement settings (on/off, action, phrase, attempt limit) instead of the first agent’s.
    • 
                                
  • Realtime agents now honour the configured “silence before agent re-engages” timing for the first check-in (previously fixed at 15 seconds).
    • 
                                
  • Provider library updates: Deepgram SDK, Google GenAI and Telnyx clients updated to their latest versions.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Silence check-ins after handoffs: fixed a bug where “are you still there?” prompts were never spoken after a call moved between agents — callers could wait in silence until the call timed out.
    • 
                                
  • End-of-silence goodbye: the goodbye message now always plays in full before the call ends (it could previously be cut off mid-sentence), and speaking during the goodbye cancels the hang-up.
    • 
                                
  • Call history accuracy: calls ended by the silence timeout are now consistently recorded with the correct end reason.
    • 
                            

                        

                        
                        

                            

                                v1.38.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Bridge greetings on silent handoffs: When a call quietly moves to another agent, the receiving agent’s Initial Greeting is now spoken word-for-word as a bridge over the changeover (silent transitions on by default; per-route tick-box to turn it off, e.g. where a call loops back to the entry agent). A route’s Bridge Phrase is now spoken automatically and reliably by the system — no longer left to the AI to remember — and replaces the greeting on that route. Keep bridge lines to one short phrase. Note: silent transfers stay quiet by default.
    • 
                                
  • New voices & models: ElevenLabs V3 Conversational text-to-speech, Deepgram Flux Multilingual speech-to-text, and the LiveKit Agents 1.7.1 runtime family.
    • 
                                
  • n8n Failsafe Workflow Wizard (Reports): one-click generation of a lost-lead safety-net workflow that emails you when a call ends without being handled.
    • 
                                
  • Webhook tool guardrails: required-field guards are now enforced on webhook tools, with live agent thinking-state feedback and a new activity visualizer.
    • 
                                
  • Safer LiveKit server upgrades: the Server tab’s upgrade button now backs up first, health-checks the new version, and rolls back automatically if it fails to start.
    • 
                                
  • Clinic Front Desk template plus phone-voice delivery rules and hesitant-caller tuning across templates; voiced chat widgets now automatically follow spoken-reply delivery rules.
    • 
                                
  • Community Edition: a free tier (2 voice agents + 2 chatbot agents) with its own Licensing tab in Settings.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Speech recognition now survives agent handoffs: the recovery system follows the call to the new agent — a dead speech-recognition connection after a handoff reconnects or switches to your configured backup within seconds, instead of leaving the agent unable to hear (previously this could end the call). 
    • 
                                
  • Privacy: the dashboard now instructs search engines not to index it.
    • 
                                
  • Note for QA/testing: simulation and Improvement Lab scores for agents using silent transitions aren’t comparable across this update (calls now contain bridge audio) — re-baseline after updating.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • “Voice change on a transition” false alarm: the warning no longer flags agents that speak with the identical voice stored in two different config formats; real voice mismatches still warn.
    • 
                                
  • Recordings page: deleting a call with a recording now refreshes the page correctly, and header buttons no longer collapse the sections.
    • 
                                
  • Exports: agent names with special characters no longer break the export download; the web-chat top export button is now labelled “Export All”.
    • 
                                
  • UI polish: file downloads no longer strand the loading overlay, limit-blocked Create buttons explain why when clicked, and badge/button colours fixed on dark theme.
    • 
                            

                        

                        
                        

                            

                                v1.37.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Agent Handoffs overhauled (Transfers & Transitions): Chained handoffs now work — an agent reached by a handoff gets its own onward handoff options, so multi-step designs (reception → booking → back to reception) function end to end. The AI-generated summary context mode now genuinely writes an AI handover brief at the moment of transfer, with a per-target choice of which model writes it and optional custom instructions (adds a short pause, typically 2–5 seconds). Silent handoffs no longer replay the next agent’s greeting. A new Transfers & Transitions User Guide page explains both design styles with ready-to-use example prompts.
    • 
                                
  • Handoff voice-change warning: The agent editor now warns when any transition in the chain would audibly change the voice mid-call — including hops configured on other agents’ pages.
    • 
                                
  • Reasoning control for more Bedrock models: The Reasoning effort dropdown now works on GPT-OSS 120B/20B (always reason — Off pins their lightest, fastest setting) and on Qwen3, GLM, DeepSeek, Nemotron and Kimi (High switches real thinking on). The hint under the dropdown explains each model’s behaviour.
    • 
                                
  • Transfer summary on call records: Call history now records a summary of attended/blind transfers made during the call.
    • 
                                
  • Multi-day log viewing & log retention: The per-agent Logs button and the Settings log viewer can now search back through older log files (including compressed ones), and a new Log Files panel under Settings › System lets you choose how long diagnostic logs are kept (default 60 days) with automatic tidy-up so logs can no longer fill the disk.
    • 
                                
  • End a web session from your own page: Sites embedding the agent via the token API can now close the call’s room the moment the visitor disconnects, so the next Connect always starts fresh.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • More accurate call costs: Bedrock Claude models on AU/Regional routing now bill at AWS’s regional rate (10% above Global), and Deepgram speech-to-text uses per-model rates. Call Detail shows the stored cost breakdown per component.
    • 
                                
  • Speech-to-text resilience: Dead speech-recognition streams are detected and replaced much faster, with smarter escalation when a provider keeps failing mid-call.
    • 
                                
  • Agent Tester clarity: Text mode now shows a reminder that typing only tests the language model and tools — not your speech provider or voice — and points you to Voice mode for the speech side.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Duplicate handoffs: An interrupted handoff could fire twice in a row; a guard now prevents repeats, and a per-call safety cap stops accidental handoff loops.
    • 
                                
  • Call diagnostics retention: Fixed several edge cases where stored call diagnostics could report the wrong retention tier.
    • 
                                
  • General stability and housekeeping fixes.
    • 
                            

                        

                        
                        

                            

                                v1.36.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Tronic Support Access: A new switch on Settings › Integrations › MCP Server that lets Tronic support securely connect to your dashboard to diagnose a problem — instead of copying logs back and forth. Off by default, turns itself off after 7 days, and everything support does is recorded. There’s nothing to configure — just switch it on when you need help.
    • 
                                
  • Mode-aware Agent & Chatbot Templates: The starter templates now adapt to the kind of agent you’re building, covering eight common scenarios so new agents start closer to what you need.
    • 
                                
  • GoHighLevel Wizard & MCP Templates: New GoHighLevel cards in the tool wizard plus ready-to-use GHL and n8n MCP templates for faster CRM integrations.
    • 
                                
  • New AI Models (August 2026): A fresh batch of AWS Bedrock and Google Gemini models, including Grok 4.6 on Bedrock, plus a reasoning-effort scale for models that support it. The new SLNG provider adds six more models with automatic region routing.
    • 
                                
  • CDN & Access (installs behind a CDN or load balancer): A new Settings › Server section for dashboards that sit behind a CDN or load balancer — correct visitor-IP handling and an option to refuse traffic that bypassed the CDN.
    • 
                                
  • Invoice History: Invoicing now keeps a history of issued invoices with stored copies and a Re-send action, plus a Preview button to check an invoice before it goes out.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • AWS Bedrock Service Tier: The Service Tier setting now works correctly and can never interrupt a call, with a Reasoning-effort dropdown where the model supports it.
    • 
                                
  • Measured Model Speeds: Model dropdowns now show speed ratings from a fresh performance sweep to help you pick the right one.
    • 
                                
  • Clearer Server Tab: The Server tab now labels the connection field “LiveKit/SIP URL” and shows it as a clean host address.
    • 
                                
  • MCP Secret Masking: MCP server secrets are hidden from view-only users.
    • 
                                
  • Steadier Alerts: Important status alerts now stay on screen instead of auto-dismissing, and Settings tooltips are back.
    • 
                                
  • Finance Tab: Pricing and Invoicing are combined into one Finance area with clearer sub-tabs.
    • 
                                
  • Dependency updates: Refreshed supporting libraries.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Update Recovery Page: The “please wait” page shown during an update now correctly detects when the dashboard is back and reloads.
    • 
                                
  • Invoicing Reliability: Closed two paths to a duplicate invoice email, stopped a double-click on Re-send from emailing twice, made the nightly invoice check resilient to a single bad day, and ensured a backup restore can never un-issue an invoice a customer already has.
    • 
                                
  • Stability behind a CDN: Fixed cases where requests could be re-processed and where access controls behaved incorrectly for installs behind a CDN or load balancer.
    • 
                                
  • Security improvements.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.35.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • n8n Webhook Wizard: A guided wizard (Tools → Add Tool) that builds a webhook tool and a matching ready-to-import n8n workflow together — with templates for support tickets, team notifications, Google Sheets, Cal.com calendar booking, and a website AI demo funnel.
    • 
                                
  • Call Recording Audio Options: Choose how recordings are made — mixed or separated caller/agent channels, a quality tier, and a space-saving OGG format (roughly half the file size). Recording format now lives in the same Call Recording Audio card.
    • 
                                
  • SIP Codec Selection & Media Timeout: Lock any trunk to specific audio codecs and set a media inactivity timeout, available on every trunk form and via MCP.
    • 
                                
  • Call Audio Processing: New Settings → Storage section controlling the agent’s input audio rate — install-wide or per agent — which can halve noise-cancellation CPU cost on busy servers.
    • 
                                
  • Dashboard IP Lock: A Settings → Security option to restrict dashboard access to a list of approved IP addresses.
    • 
                                
  • Output Volume: A per-agent volume slider for the agent’s voice, on both voice and chatbot agents.
    • 
                                
  • Tool Usage Instructions: Every tool can now carry its own usage guidance telling the AI when and how to use it, on voice and chatbot agents.
    • 
                                
  • Improvement Lab Caller-Only Replay: Transcription tests on dual-channel recordings can replay just the caller’s side, giving more realistic accuracy scores — with a warning when the reference under-covers the audio.
    • 
                                
  • Simulation & AutoResearch via MCP: 28 new MCP tools so external integrations can run simulations, review results, and manage AutoResearch.
    • 
                                
  • One-click Copy Buttons: Copy results straight from Simulation, Improvement Lab, and AutoResearch screens.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Voice Runtime Update: LiveKit Agents updated to 1.6.9 with refreshed AI provider SDKs (OpenAI, Anthropic, ElevenLabs, and more).
    • 
                                
  • Echo Cancel Warmup Auto: The warmup default now adapts to how the call arrives, so phone and web calls each get the right setting automatically.
    • 
                                
  • User Guide: Field-by-field coverage of the Storage tab and the new Call Audio Processing section, plus a refreshed agent-editor Model Guide.
    • 
                                
  • Recording Waveforms: The waveform display now reflects all recording channels, not just the first.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Speech Recognition Accuracy: Fixed a long-standing audio-processing fault where noise cancellation could corrupt a significant share of the caller’s speech before it reached transcription — the root cause of clearly-spoken words being misheard. If your agents use noise cancellation, expect noticeably better recognition.
    • 
                                
  • SIP Trunk Safety: Adding or removing numbers and editing trunks no longer wipes the trunk’s stored password or silently changes its transport setting.
    • 
                                
  • Recording Cleanup: Deleting calls now reliably removes their recordings (including a background sweeper for files that were previously left behind), and delete results report what actually happened.
    • 
                                
  • Hangup Polish: The agent’s goodbye is no longer clipped mid-word on phone calls, and two dead-air pauses around hangup and tool use are gone.
    • 
                                
  • Greeting Reliability: Realtime agents no longer skip their greeting when the caller starts talking the moment the call connects.
    • 
                                
  • Agent Tester: Voice-mode tests could silently fail to hear you after a browser library update — fixed; text-mode sessions no longer crash on start.
    • 
                                
  • Chatbot Summaries: AI call summaries now pick up data-extraction fields from chatbot agents.
    • 
                                
  • AutoResearch: No longer returns empty results when using OpenAI or Azure reasoning models.
    • 
                                
  • Editor Saves: Saving an agent no longer resets Audio Detector Patience or drops two advanced Flux support settings.
    • 
                                
  • Storage Settings: Saving storage settings is now crash-safe — concurrent saves can no longer corrupt the configuration.
    • 
                                
  • Security improvements.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.34.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Speech Recognition Stall Recovery: An optional safety ladder for voice agents (agent editor → Speech Recognition). If the transcription provider stops responding mid-call, the agent can now restart it, switch to a backup transcription provider you choose, and — as a last resort — say a polite goodbye instead of leaving the caller in dead air.
    • 
                                
  • Create Simulation Tests from Real Calls: Turn any past call into a repeatable test with one click, replay it exactly, and compare runs side-by-side in the new Replay Workbench — including rerunning a single turn to try a different wording.
    • 
                                
  • Simulation Deep Evaluation & Prompt Improvement: Simulations can now be scored in depth, generate a suggested prompt revision from every test’s findings, run A/B suites across prompt versions, and apply the winning version to the live agent with a deliberate Apply-to-Live step. You can also pick which AI model plays the caller, per suite.
    • 
                                
  • AutoResearch Page: AutoResearch now has its own page in the sidebar. It harvests problem calls, suggests prompt improvements with guardrails, and lets you test a suggestion in Simulation before applying it.
    • 
                                
  • Email Reports for Simulation & Improvement Lab: Both can now send email reports with the full result of every test, on their own triggers and templates.
    • 
                                
  • Chatbot Upgrades: AI summaries and data extraction for text conversations; a per-chatbot session length limit; a reconnect grace period so a dropped visitor can pick up where they left off; per-session dynamic variables; a session Logs button; and welcome messages for web chat and SMS.
    • 
                                
  • New Voice Models & Providers: SCX (Au) speech-to-text, AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro, xAI Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 with reasoning and speed controls, and an OpenRouter refresh adding Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash and free community models (with clear warnings about their limits).
    • 
                                
  • Voicemail Recording Playback: Voicemail detection can now play an uploaded recording instead of a spoken message.
    • 
                                
  • Stop Recording at Transfer: Call recording can automatically stop when a call is transferred to a human (on by default; per-tool toggle).
    • 
                                
  • Timezone Everywhere + Scheduled STT Lab Runs: Every date and time in the dashboard now follows the timezone set in Settings → Server, and Improvement Lab transcription tests can run on a schedule.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Voice Runtime Update: LiveKit Agents updated to 1.6.8 with refreshed provider SDKs, plus a new diagnostic that flags transcription timeouts.
    • 
                                
  • User Guide Refresh: Every screenshot re-shot, a field-level accuracy pass over every chapter, a new Improvement Lab chapter, and a button that deep-links to the guide chapter for the page you’re on.
    • 
                                
  • Smarter Editors: The chatbot editor greys out speech models whose SDK or API key is missing, and the free-model warning now also covers the two fallback model slots.
    • 
                                
  • Indian Rupee Support: INR added as a display currency, and a missing exchange rate is now fetched automatically when you save a currency.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Calls Crashing Before the Greeting: Fixed a critical bug where real phone calls could fail immediately, before the agent spoke.
    • 
                                
  • Billing Accuracy: Call costs are now recorded against the AI model that actually answered, including when a fallback model stepped in.
    • 
                                
  • Export/Import Completeness: Agent export/import no longer drops 13 configuration settings, and chatbot agents keep their per-provider speech settings.
    • 
                                
  • Recording Status Truthfulness: Recording labels now reflect what actually happened, and a dead-air tail at the end of some recordings is gone.
    • 
                                
  • Azure Realtime Transcription: Caller transcription now works with Azure realtime agents.
    • 
                                
  • Simulation Reliability: Suite runs no longer hang at “running” after a dashboard restart, and a chatbot greeting is no longer saved twice to chat history.
    • 
                                
  • Security improvements.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.33.1
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • ai‐coustics Speech Detection: Voice agents using ai‐coustics noise cancellation can now also use ai‐coustics as their Speech Detection Engine (agent editor → Voice Activity Controls). It listens only to the main caller — a TV or someone talking in the background won’t trigger or interrupt the agent. If the engine is ever unavailable, the agent automatically falls back to the standard detector so calls always keep working.
    • 
                                
  • Hide User Guide per user: Admins can now hide the yellow User Guide button for individual team logins (Users → Access & Display).
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Clearer ai‐coustics model choices: The enhancement‐model list now says plainly what each model does (QUAIL‐L keeps every voice; Voice Focus isolates the main speaker) and reflects current ai‐coustics licensing — all models are included, billed per processed minute. The Dependencies tab also now notifies you when a new ai‐coustics plugin version is available.
    • 
                                
  • Turn Detector clarity with Flux: While Deepgram Flux turn detection is on, the Turn Detector controls grey out to show Flux is handling end‐of‐turn — your saved choice is kept and comes back when Flux is switched off.
    • 
                                
  • Smoother updates: The LiveKit server upgrade check recovers better from slow restarts, and a friendlier “dashboard is restarting” page shows during updates.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Call Detail noise‐cancellation status: Calls were incorrectly labelled “failed, ran without” even when noise cancellation ran fine — the badge now reflects reality.
    • 
                                
  • Stuck editor notices: Several agent‐editor warning notes (including the Flux end‐of‐turn note) could stay visible when they no longer applied — they now appear and disappear correctly.
    • 
                                
  • Connection test timing: The LiveKit connection test no longer reports 0.0 ms when a connection attempt fails partway.
    • 
                                
  • Security improvements.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.33.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Built‐in User Guide: A complete, plain‐English user guide is now built right into the dashboard — open it any time from the yellow User Guide button in the top bar. It walks new users all the way from logging in to a live agent answering a real phone call: a first‐time setup checklist, a five‐step quick start, and a chapter for every page (Voice & Chatbot Agents, Knowledge Base, Tools, Telephony, Analytics, Reports and more), each with screenshots you can click to enlarge. It also includes tips on writing a good agent prompt, a troubleshooting FAQ, and a glossary of the jargon. The guide is white‐labeled with your own dashboard name, and admin‐only Settings chapters are automatically hidden from team logins that don’t have Settings access.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Model Speed Ratings: The newest Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash‐Lite models now show speed star ratings in the agent editor, so you can pick a fast model at a glance.
    • 
                                
  • Clearer Editor Wording: Reworded the dependencies notice in the agent editor so it’s easier to understand.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.32.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Improvement Lab: A new workspace for improving your agents from real calls. Replay call recordings through different speech‐recognition and noise‐cancellation combinations to find the most accurate setup, score call outcomes against your own success criteria with AI judges, get AI‐drafted prompt improvements, and lock in quality with repeatable audio regression tests (including a one‐click “run all”). Every run shows an itemised cost estimate up front, results appear on the Call Detail page, and Lab data is included in system backups.
    • 
                                
  • Improvement Lab via API/MCP: External AI assistants connected through the dashboard’s built‐in MCP server can now drive the full improvement loop — diagnosing calls, running scoring, and proposing prompt updates — with the same safeguards as the dashboard UI.
    • 
                                
  • New Google Models: Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash‐Lite are now available for voice agents, chatbots and AI summaries — on both Google AI Studio and Vertex AI.
    • 
                                
  • Service Alert Grace Period: Service‐down email alerts now support a configurable delay, so brief restarts don’t trigger unnecessary notifications.
    • 
                                
  • Capacity Node Offline Alerts: Multi‐Cluster installs now send an email alert when a capacity node goes offline.
    • 
                                
  • Voice Pipeline on Call Detail: The Call Detail page now shows which noise‐cancellation setting was active on each call, alongside the rest of the voice pipeline.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Sandbox Moved into Settings: The Sandbox now lives under Settings › Integrations/API (admin‐only), keeping the main navigation cleaner.
    • 
                                
  • Cleaner Call History: Removed the rarely‐used End Reason column for a tidier table.
    • 
                                
  • Noise Cancellation Polish: The strength slider now applies correctly across noise‐cancellation providers, with sensible per‐provider defaults.
    • 
                                
  • Agent Tester Clarity: Chatbot test runs now clearly show which model the chatbot used.
    • 
                                
  • Updated AI Provider Libraries: Refreshed the OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Cartesia libraries, plus the LiveKit agents runtime — bringing the latest provider fixes and model support.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Webhook Tool Names: Clearer validation message when a webhook tool name isn’t valid, checked as you type.
    • 
                                
  • Security Improvements: Additional hardening of the dashboard’s protection systems.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.31.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Chat Widget Display Modes: The website chat widget now offers six display modes — classic bubble, sidebar, fullscreen, and minimal voice‐orb / voice‐button modes with animated visuals — plus new appearance controls (auto light/dark theme, corner styles, launcher options). The widget editor previews each mode and generates the matching embed code.
    • 
                                
  • Chatbot Agents in the Agent Tester: The Agent Tester can now run scripted test conversations against Chatbot Agents, not just voice agents.
    • 
                                
  • Smarter Chatbot Webhooks: Chatbot webhook tools can now receive the visitor’s phone number and session ID automatically, and each chatbot has a configurable reply for when a webhook fails.
    • 
                                
  • Separate History Retention Controls: Call history, chat history and recordings now each have their own retention setting (local and cloud independently), defaulting to keep‐forever, with a configurable daily clean‐up time.
    • 
                                
  • Claude Sonnet 5 (Regional) on Amazon Bedrock: New regional model option that follows your configured Bedrock region settings.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Much Faster Replies on Noisy Phone Lines: Voice agents using Deepgram Nova speech recognition now respond up to 10× sooner after the caller stops speaking on noisy lines (mobiles, kitchens, traffic) — removing the long pauses and “are you still there?” prompts some calls experienced.
    • 
                                
  • Echo Guard & Faster Dead‐Air Recovery (Deepgram Flux): New per‐agent Echo Guard option softens line echo that could stall speech recognition when callers talk over the agent, and the built‐in watchdog now recovers from stalls in about 3 seconds instead of 6.
    • 
                                
  • Turn‐Taking Model Auto‐Repair: The conversation turn‐taking model now installs itself automatically if its files are missing, improving how naturally agents judge when a caller has finished speaking.
    • 
                                
  • AssemblyAI Editor Polish: The Custom Prompt option is now available on the latest Universal 3.5 Pro model, and the editor clearly shows AssemblyAI’s own Key Terms field instead of the unused Custom Vocabulary box.
    • 
                                
  • Voice Editor Readability: Clearer, higher‐contrast setting chips and value badges in the Flux settings panel.
    • 
                                
  • Updated Libraries: Refreshed underlying platform libraries for stability.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Cloud Avatars Join Reliably: Virtual avatar providers can now always reach your LiveKit server (public address handling), and avatar IDs pasted without dashes are formatted automatically.
    • 
                                
  • SIP Wizard Preset: Corrected the Breeze Connect provider preset address.
    • 
                                
  • Small Fixes: Dispatch‐rules list scrolling, safer agent auto‐start behaviour, and clearer wizard and recording setup text.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.30.7
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Multi‐Cluster Mode (Capacity Nodes): A new licensed add‐on that lets you grow call capacity by joining extra “capacity node” servers to your dashboard. Add and manage nodes from Settings › Server › Multi‐Cluster with a guided join wizard, a live fleet view, and per‐node actions (approve, whitelist IP, reboot, remove). Includes room‐balancing options so new calls are spread across the least‐busy servers, an agent‐busy cutoff, optional call recording on nodes, and honest reporting of which server handled each call (shown on Call History, Call Detail and the Rooms page). Existing single‐server installs are completely unaffected.
    • 
                                
  • xAI Grok Speech Recognition & Grok 4.5: A new xAI Grok speech‐to‐text option for voice agents, plus the Grok 4.5 model — available for agents (with a reasoning‐effort control) and for AI summaries.

 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Better Turn Detection & a New Patience Setting: More reliable detection of when a caller has finished speaking, with a new per‐agent Patience control so you can tune how long the agent waits before replying.
    • 
                                
  • Security Improvements: A range of behind‐the‐scenes security hardening across the dashboard and agent.
    • 
                                
  • Updated Libraries: Refreshed underlying provider and platform libraries for stability and compatibility.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Realtime Agents Say Goodbye Before Hanging Up: When a Realtime (audio‐to‐audio) agent ends a call, it now speaks its closing line before hanging up instead of occasionally dropping the call silently.

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Deepgram Flux for Telnyx Speech Recognition: A new lowest‐latency speech‐to‐text option purpose‐built for voice agents, with built‐in end‐of‐turn detection. Choose it alongside Deepgram Nova 3 when using Telnyx AI.

  • Claude Sonnet 5 & GPT‐OSS on AWS Bedrock: Sonnet 5 (Global) plus the open‐weight GPT‐OSS 120B and 20B models are now available for Bedrock agents and AI summaries.

  • Safer Defaults for New Agents: Newly created agents now start with a 10‐minute maximum call length and automatically end a call after 60 seconds of silence. Existing agents are unchanged.

  • Dead‐Air Protection: Voice agents now detect and recover automatically if speech recognition or the voice output stalls mid‐call, instead of going silent.

  • Loading Indicator on Analytics: Changing the date range on the overview page now shows a loading indicator instead of looking frozen.
    • 
                                
  • Faster Call History & Analytics: Further speed improvements on the call history and analytics pages.

 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Outbound Test Calls Labelled Correctly: Test calls placed from the Outbound page now show as “Outbound” in Call History instead of being mislabelled as inbound.

  • Take‐a‐Message SMS: The take‐a‐message feature now reliably sends its SMS for every voice agent type.
    • 
                                
  • Call Direction Accuracy: Improved detection of caller and recipient numbers for SIP calls.
    • 
                                
  • Extended Reasoning Styling: The Extended Reasoning option for AWS Bedrock agents now matches the rest of the settings, with a clearer per‐model explanation.

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Smarter Turn Detection for Realtime Agents: Realtime (audio‐to‐audio) agents can now use an opt‐in audio turn detector that listens to the caller’s speech rhythm to judge when they’ve finished talking — runs entirely on your own server. Enable it per agent in Conversation Dynamics.
    • 
                                
  • Claude Sonnet 5: Anthropic’s new Sonnet 5 model replaces Sonnet 4.5 in the agent model list — better quality at the same speed rating.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Much Faster Dashboard: A major performance overhaul. The Home page, Call History and Chat History now open in a fraction of a second on every visit — the dashboard shows you the latest numbers instantly and refreshes them quietly in the background instead of making you wait. Heavy data work also no longer stalls the rest of the site while it runs, and pages stay fast as your call history grows.
    • 
                                
  • Updated Voice Engine & AI Providers: Upgraded the underlying voice engine and the Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Telnyx and other provider libraries for stability and compatibility.
    • 
                                
  • Leaner Nightly Backups: The nightly backup uses far less memory while it runs and captures server credentials more robustly.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Recordings Storage Display: The Home page’s recordings card was showing zero recordings and zero storage even when recordings existed. It now reports the real counts, storage size and disk usage. (Your recordings were always safe — only the display was affected.)
    • 
                                
  • “Test All Models” Accuracy: Fixed 12 model checks that reported failures for models that actually work.
    •

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Cal.com Calendar Tools: Two new agent tools let your voice agents work with a Cal.com online calendar — Check Availability looks up open appointment times, and Book makes the booking once the caller picks a time. Add them on the Tools page with your Cal.com API key and Event Type ID, set a timezone (or leave blank to use the dashboard’s), and use the Test button to confirm the connection. Works the same as the other built‐in tools, with global or per‐agent settings.
    • 
                                
  • Reasoning Effort for GPT Realtime 2: A new control lets you choose how much the GPT Realtime 2 voice model “thinks” before it responds, for both OpenAI and Azure realtime agents — trade a little latency for stronger reasoning, or keep it fast. Set it per agent in the editor.
    • 
                                
  • More Azure Realtime Voices: Added the Marin and Cedar voices for Azure GPT Realtime 2 agents.
    • 
                                
  • Custom Voicemail Detection Instructions: An optional field to add your own voicemail‐detection guidance, appended to the built‐in detection — useful for tuning how the agent recognises an answering machine.

 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Warm Standby Options: The agent warm‐standby setting now correctly honours “0” (cold start on every call) and adds higher options (3 and 4) for servers with more memory, for faster back‐to‐back call handling.
    • 
                                
  • Updated Libraries: Refreshed several underlying provider libraries (Anthropic, Deepgram and others) for stability and compatibility.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Speech‐Recognition Model Selection: Removed an unnecessary notification banner that appeared when selecting a Deepgram speech‐recognition model.
    • 
                                
  • Azure Realtime Model Check: Fixed the “Test All Models” check for Azure realtime so it probes the correct endpoint and reports accurate results.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.27.2
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Self-Hosted Smart Turn Detection: A new turn-detection option that listens for natural pauses in speech — running entirely on your own server — so the agent waits for the caller to actually finish instead of relying on a fixed timer. Makes conversations feel more natural, especially when callers pause mid-sentence. Choose it per agent in Conversation Dynamics.
    • 
                                
  • Sarvam (Indian Languages) Speech: Added Sarvam.ai as a new speech provider for Indian-language speech recognition (Saaras / Saarika) and text-to-speech (Bulbul).
    • 
                                
  • Azure GPT Realtime 2: Added Azure’s GPT Realtime 2 model plus a dedicated Azure Realtime endpoint option for realtime (audio‐to‐audio) agents.
    • 
                                
  • Lock Summaries: A new setting to lock call summaries so they can’t be accidentally edited or regenerated once finalised.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Updated Voice Engine & AI Providers: Upgraded the underlying voice engine and the OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, ElevenLabs and Telnyx libraries for better stability and compatibility.
    • 
                                
  • Realtime Agents Start More Reliably: Realtime (audio‐to‐audio) agents no longer need separate text-model or transcription keys configured just to start up.
    • 
                                
  • Clearer Realtime Guidance: The editor now flags that Gemini 3.x Live realtime is higher‐latency, so you can choose the right model for your use case.
    • 
                                
  • Azure Speech Settings: Azure Speech keys now save and persist reliably with a clear “Set” indicator, and the settings layout was tidied up.

  • Security Improvements: A range of behind‐the‐scenes security hardening across the dashboard.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Keypad (DTMF) Collection: Fixed collecting phone‐keypad digits from callers so it works reliably and is recorded in the call transcript.
    • 
                                
  • Smarter Silence Detection: The agent no longer mistakenly treats a call as “silent” and ends or re‐prompts while it is still speaking, thinking, or running a tool.
    • 
                                
  • Favicon Console Error: Fixed a harmless browser console error by serving the site icon correctly.

                                v1.26.1
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Choose Your Noise Cancellation: Each agent now has a Noise Cancellation dropdown in Conversation Dynamics. Pick Off, WebRTC APM (very low CPU, tuned for phone‐call audio — the recommended everyday choice), DTLN (stronger neural filtering), or ai|coustics (premium). Every option runs entirely on your own server. Existing agents are unchanged unless you pick an option.
    • 
                                
  • ai|coustics Premium Noise Cancellation: Optional premium speech enhancement that can isolate the main speaker and strip out other voices in the background. Add your SDK licence key under Settings → Integrations — with a one‐click Test button that confirms the key is valid — then install the plugin from the Dependencies tab.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • SIP Setup Wizard Provider Logos: The SIP trunk setup wizard now shows each provider’s logo on its tile for easier recognition, and adds a Breeze Connect provider preset.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Noise Cancellation Call Quality Under Load: Fixed audio breaking up and poor quality when two or more calls used noise cancellation at the same time. The previous engine could overload the server’s processors under concurrent calls; it now runs efficiently, and the new lighter WebRTC APM option handles many simultaneous calls comfortably.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.26.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Text‐Mode Simulations: Agent simulations can now run as fast text conversations instead of full voice calls — the agent’s complete logic (prompts, tools, knowledge base, handoffs) is tested in a fraction of the time and cost. Voice mode remains available for end‐to‐end audio testing.
    • 
                                
  • Simulation Test Suites: Group test cases into suites, run the whole suite as a parallel batch, and compare results run‐over‐run to spot regressions after a prompt or config change.
    • 
                                
  • AI Judges & Caller Personas: Simulations can be scored per dimension (accuracy, tone, task completion) by an AI judge, and simulated callers can adopt personas — impatient, confused, chatty — for more realistic testing. AI test‐case generation is persona‐ and judge‐aware.
    • 
                                
  • New Voice Provider — SLNG.ai: Speech‐to‐text and text‐to‐speech support, with regional endpoints and per‐minute pricing.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Call Diagnostics Storage Overhaul: Diagnostic data (timelines and traces) for recent calls now lives in fast memory for a configurable window (default 7 days, with a hard size limit), while local files and cloud storage each get their own retention period — cloud archives can be kept for a year by default. This dramatically reduces database memory on busy servers; older calls load from the archive automatically when opened.
    • 
                                
  • Storage Usage Gauges: Settings → Storage now shows live Archive Usage and Redis Usage readouts, and the usage gauge fills itself in instead of showing “calculating…” until refreshed.
    • 
                                
  • Smarter Storage Settings: Retention fields that don’t apply to your storage setup grey out automatically, and cloud‐only archiving is now the default when cloud storage is configured.
    • 
                                
  • Simulation Page Redesign: Reorganised into Suites, Test Cases and Results tabs with a clearer introduction.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Diagnostics Cleanup on Cloud Storage: Retention cleanup for call diagnostics now runs on schedule for cloud‐storage installs (previously it only ran at restart) and works correctly when local copies are disabled.
    • 
                                
  • Simulation Call‐Control Tools: Hang‐up and transfer tools no longer error inside simulations — they return simulated success so test conversations complete naturally.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.25.5
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Attended Transfers — Agent Can Now Hear the Destination: During the private consultation the agent couldn’t hear the person being transferred to, so “yes, put them through” did nothing. The agent now hears and responds to the destination, and completing the transfer connects both parties correctly.
    • 
                                
  • Attended Transfers — Hold Music: Callers on hold heard silence (the music was far too quiet and stopped after about a minute), while the transfer destination heard the hold music instead. Music now plays clearly to the caller only, loops for the whole hold, and the volume slider behaves like a real volume knob.
    • 
                                
  • Attended Transfers — After a Failed Transfer: When the destination’s voicemail picked up or the consultation timed out, the agent could return and talk to the caller as if they were the transfer destination, or give the wrong reason (“voicemail picked up” after a timeout). The agent now returns with an accurate, polite explanation and resumes the conversation normally.
    • 
                                
  • Hold Music Selection: The Hold Music dropdown in an agent’s tool settings was empty. You can now choose built‐in clips or your uploaded files per agent (applies to both the attended transfer and hold tools), and the currently saved choice displays correctly.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • No More Mid‐Transfer Interruptions: The agent no longer asks “are you still there?” while a transfer is in progress.
    • 
                                
  • Transfer Timeout Behaviour: If a consultation runs out of time, the agent now apologises to the caller straight away instead of staying silent. The timeout setting’s help text also explains that dialling time counts toward the limit.
    • 
                                
  • Component Update: Refreshed the Telnyx SMS connector.
    •

 Bug Fixes

  • Dispatch Rule Safety: Saving a dispatch rule now validates that the selected agent actually exists, so a rule can no longer be saved pointing at a deleted agent.

 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Telephony Reliability: Behind‐the‐scenes hardening of dispatch‐rule and SIP‐trunk management for more predictable saves.

  • Telnyx Native Transcription Fix: The Telnyx engine in the Telnyx speech‐to‐text menu could silently produce no transcripts because of how it handles language settings. It now transcribes correctly in every region.

 Improvements

 New Features

 New Features

 New Features

An optional setting adds the full technical request and response details for deeper auditing. Just tick the new fields in your webhook report settings.
    • 
                                
  • Dispatch Rule Guidance: The Agent Management banner now links straight to the Dispatch Rules page and clearly flags when a dispatch rule is required.

 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Dismissible Status Alerts: The yellow “agent stopped” warning and the information banners can now be dismissed for the session.
    • 
                                
  • Smarter Dependencies Tab: The Dependencies tab now shows only upgrades that can actually be installed, hiding ones that aren’t reachable.
    • 
                                
  • Clearer Delete Confirmations: Larger, easier‐to‐read pop‐ups when deleting calls or chats, with corrected colours and responsive sizing.
    • 
                                
  • More Accurate Text‐Chat Costs: Text‐only chats no longer show phantom speech‐to‐text or text‐to‐speech cost estimates.
    • 
                                
  • Updated Core Components: Refreshed the underlying LiveKit voice runtime and other core platform components for stability.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Agent Tester Clarity: The tester now clearly tells you when an agent isn’t started, instead of failing silently.

  • Recordings Delete: Honest “delete with recordings” handling, a clearer no‐recording badge, and a fixed bulk‐delete spinner.

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Smarter Call Health Scoring: Call health now uses continuous latency‐based scoring and only rates calls that had a genuine back‐and‐forth conversation. Calls without enough caller interaction now show a neutral “Not scored” state instead of a misleading number, and you can filter Call History by Not Scored.
    • 
                                
  • Call History — Call ID Search & Easier Navigation: A new Call ID column with a copy button and search‐by‐Call‐ID, a Back button, and reorganised single‐line filters (Search moved to the front) with horizontal scrolling for wide tables.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Much Faster Page Loading: The Home/Overview, Call History, Chat History and Recordings pages now load quickly and smoothly even with large histories, across all storage backends. The first login after a restart is noticeably faster too.
    • 
                                
  • Accurate Analytics: The Analytics tab now shows real SIP and call‐ingress figures (these previously displayed placeholder values), with corrected labels, date‐range handling and currency display. The Room Trends section was tidied into a cleaner, more consistent layout.
    • 
                                
  • Better Knowledge Base Answers: The default Answer Synthesis prompt was improved for more accurate, better‐grounded answers — applied automatically, no action needed.
    • 
                                
  • Tidier History Tables: Cleaner, better‐sized columns on Call History; the voice Agent filter now lists voice agents only, and the Chat History Agent filter lists chatbot agents only.

 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Call Health in Exports: The call‐health score in JSON exports now matches what the dashboard shows on screen.
    • 
                                
  • Reliable Call ID Copy: Copying a Call ID now works reliably even on rapid repeated clicks.
    • 
                                
  • Security & Access Hardening: Tightened access controls on call recordings and downloads (security improvements).

Upstream fixes only — including improved AWS Bedrock tool handling and a SIP answering‐machine‐detection timing fix — plus assorted plugin reliability improvements. The Telnyx SMS library was also refreshed. No breaking changes for existing agents.

The saved Extended Reasoning setting is also no longer cleared when reopening an agent.

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Azure OpenAI — Major Expansion: The Azure integration now supports a separate endpoint for each service (Language model, Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech), 19 selectable Azure language models, 39 Azure voices, and per-service Show/Hide toggles so you can display only the Azure services you actually use. The provider is now simply labelled “Azure”, and GPT-5.4 / GPT-5.5 were added to the AI-summary model list. Existing Azure agents keep working with no changes needed.
    • 
                                
  • Backup & Restore — Much Safer Restores: Before any restore overwrites your live data, the dashboard now takes a full pre-restore safety snapshot and automatically rolls back to it if the restore fails partway through. The restore confirmation shows exactly what will be replaced, and a new Undo last restore button lets you reverse a restore you didn’t intend to run. Restores now also refuse to wipe your data when the selected backup is empty, and the dashboard restarts its services automatically when a restore finishes. The Backup tab loads your schedule and cloud backups as soon as you open it.

 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Updated AI Provider Libraries: Refreshed the Anthropic (Claude), ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Google GenAI (Gemini / Vertex) and Agent Memory libraries to their latest versions, along with the Telnyx SMS library and several underlying components (including a security update to form handling). Bug fixes and small improvements only — no breaking changes for existing agents.

  • Clearer Endpointing Help: The voice agent editor now explains the Dynamic vs Fixed endpointing modes in plain English, making it easier to choose how the agent decides you’ve finished speaking.
    • 
                                
  • Model Catalog Accuracy: Corrected the Gemini 2.5 (AI Studio) retirement dates, added GPT-5.5 to the AI-summary list, and made model handling more robust against provider-side changes.

  • Performance & Quieter Logs: Added an optional preemptive-speech setting (off by default) and reduced noisy per-turn log output.

 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • SIP Dispatch Rules: Several fixes — editing a rule no longer clears its room settings when the agent field is left blank; the time profile and auto-record options now save correctly on rules that don’t pin a specific agent; a stale agent reference is cleared when you choose “No Agent”; and the agent shown on the SIP Inbound page is now correct.
    • 
                                
  • Call Health on Short Calls: Speech-to-Text health now appears even on very short calls and is based on the real transcription delay rather than the voice-activity gap, giving a more accurate reading.
    • 
                                
  • AI Summary Dropdowns: The summary provider and model pickers in Settings no longer get stuck showing “Loading…”.

    • 
                                
  • Backup Connection Settings: Fixed a case where restoring a backup could mismatch the saved database connection settings.

 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • LiveKit Voice Engine Update (1.5.12 → 1.5.13): Bumped the core voice‐agent runtime and all twenty LiveKit provider plugins (Deepgram, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Google, AWS, Anthropic, xAI, Groq, Azure, Hume, AssemblyAI, Speechmatics, MiniMax, D‐ID, Tavus, Bey, LiveAvatar, Silero, Turn Detector) to 1.5.13. Patch‐level upstream fixes — a fix for a rare race that could drop the tail of an interruption, more reliable voice‐activity detection, smoother background audio (fade in/out), and assorted plugin reliability fixes. No breaking changes for self‐hosted installs.

 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Webhook Tools — List/Object Fields Now Send Correctly: If you configured a webhook tool with a parameter typed Array or Object, the agent was sending it as quoted text instead of a real list/object, which strict APIs (for example appointment‐booking or CRM endpoints) rejected. These parameters are now sent as proper JSON arrays/objects. Tip: for best results, describe what each item contains in the parameter’s description.
    • 
                                
  • “Are You Still There?” No Longer Talks Over Itself: The silence prompt (and end‐call‐on‐silence) is now suppressed while the agent is busy running a tool or action, so it won’t interrupt mid‐task.

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Custom Silence Prompt: The Voice Agent editor’s “When the caller is silent, the agent should:” dropdown now has a new Custom option. When you pick it, a textarea appears where you can type the exact phrase the agent should say after a silence gap (up to 500 characters). Standard pipelines speak the text verbatim; realtime audio‐to‐audio agents receive it as guidance and may paraphrase. The existing three options (ask if still there, end call, stay silent) are unchanged.

Updates the agent editor STT/TTS dropdowns, the Integrations card, the Saved API Keys list, the Dependencies tab, the Pricing tab, and the MCP help tooltip. Display‐only change — any existing agents using this provider keep working with no reconfiguration needed.

Any agents in your dashboard currently configured with either model are automatically switched to sonic-3 (the closest equivalent that retains speed and volume controls) on first restart after this update. No action needed on your part. You can change the model afterwards in the voice agent editor if you prefer one of the other newly‐available variants.

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Host + Per-Service Resource Alerts: Get notified by email when your server’s CPU or memory is unusually high for a sustained period, OR when any individual service (agent worker, LiveKit, Redis, etc.) is hammering its own CPU/memory limit even when the host looks idle. Two new alert categories on Settings › Email › Notifications, alongside the existing Service Down Alerts card. Defaults: 90% sustained for 5 minutes with a 60-minute cooldown between repeat emails. You can enable host-level alerts, per-service alerts, or both.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Smarter Agent Worker CPU Recommendation: The Agent Worker CPU quota recommendation on Settings › System Resources now scales with both your server’s vCPU count and how many concurrent calls you’ve configured. Hosts with more cores and busier traffic get higher recommended quotas, which prevents the agent from being throttled when handling multiple simultaneous calls.
    • 
                                
  • Agent Diagnostics: If the agent worker stalls for more than 15 seconds (a sign of resource exhaustion), the agent now writes a snapshot to logs/agent-freeze.log so support can pinpoint exactly where it stalled. Added a similar warning when the agent worker keeps oscillating between “available” and “unavailable”, which helps spot capacity issues before they cause missed calls. Detection only — does not affect call performance.
    • 
                                
  • LiveKit Agents Update: Bumped the core voice-agent runtime (livekit-agents) and all twenty LiveKit provider plugins (Deepgram, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Google, AWS, Anthropic, xAI, Groq, Azure, Hume, AssemblyAI, Speechmatics, MiniMax, D-ID, Tavus, Bey, LiveAvatar, Silero, Turn Detector) from version 1.5.10 to 1.5.12. Patch‐level bump containing upstream bug fixes (incorrect interruption guard, Soniox plugin reliability) and additive features (longer-user-speech limit options, avatar join/playback latency metrics, new model identifiers). Also refreshed the Google AI SDK (google-genai) from 2.3 to 2.5. No breaking changes for self-hosted installs.
    • 
                                
  • Library Refresh: Bumped four underlying Python libraries to their latest patches: aiohttp (the async HTTP client used for outbound AI provider calls), litellm (the multi-provider LLM client), telnyx (the Telnyx SMS provider used by SMS-channel Chatbot Agents), and the disposable-email-domains data list (used on tenant signup pages). No user-facing behaviour changes — bug fixes only.

The dashboard now reads the version directly from the installed Python environment instead of from the package lockfile.

It now installs the bundled package correctly. (2) The updater will no longer downgrade a Python package on your server when your installed version is already newer than the one in the release. This was previously causing the OpenAI library to be silently rolled back on installs that had been kept up‐to‐date manually.

 Improvements

 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Caller Phone Now Reaches Webhook Tools After Handoff: Fixed a bug where webhook tools (CRM lookups, callback requests, blind/warm transfers) called from a handed‐off agent were receiving an empty caller‐phone field, even though the agent prompt still knew the correct number. Any tool relying on the auto‐injected caller_phone system parameter — including Caller‐ID forwarding on transfers and the built‐in callback tool — will now reliably see the caller’s original number after a handoff.

External MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) can now create and update webhook tools with control over error‐handling phrasing (speak_on_error), retry policy (count, delay, status codes), per‐session and per‐minute rate limits, business‐hours scheduling, mock‐mode for testing, and JSONPath‐based success/error conditions.  New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Branded “Restarting…” Page: When the dashboard restarts mid‐update, visitors no longer see nginx’s generic 502 error. They now see a friendly page that matches your white‐label branding (logo, dashboard name, theme colours) and auto‐refreshes once the dashboard is back up. The page is wired into nginx automatically on first boot — no manual setup needed.
    • 
                                
  • Per‐Provider Show/Hide Slider on Integrations: Every provider card on Settings › Integrations now has a Show/Hide toggle. Hide providers you’ll never use (e.g. providers without API keys, or ones outside your region) and they disappear from voice‐agent and chatbot editor dropdowns — cleaning up the model picker for your team. Toggle them back on any time. Last visible LLM/STT/TTS card is protected so you can’t accidentally hide every provider in a category.
    • 
                                
  • Self‐Serve Password Setup: Operators receiving a fresh invite or password reset can now set their password directly from the email link — no more bouncing through a separate “set up your account” flow. Old reset links that have expired now show a clear “link expired” message with a one‐click resend button instead of failing silently.
    • 
                                
  • Dependencies Tab Auto‐Tracker: The Settings › Dependencies tab now auto‐tracks new plugins and shows newer versions available for each one. Click Upgrade next to any package to install the latest version, with live progress shown as each dependency installs (no more silent multi‐minute pauses).
    • 
                                
  • Per‐Mode System Resource Suggestions: The System Resources page now gives tailored RAM and CPU suggestions based on whether your install is voice‐only, hybrid, or chat‐only — so you know exactly what your dashboard needs before scaling up.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Security Tab Consolidated: The in‐page password change form has been removed from Settings › Security — password changes now flow through the standard self‐serve reset link, eliminating a parallel UI that was easy to misuse. Widget Abuse Protection has been promoted to the top of the tab so it’s easier to find.
    • 
                                
  • AWS Bedrock Region Info Moved: The geo‐located Bedrock model availability info panel has been moved from Dependencies to Settings › Integrations next to the Bedrock card, where it belongs.
    • 
                                
  • Hardware‐ID Cached Across Updates: Customer licence validation now reads the hardware ID from a local cache file instead of re‐detecting it every time the dashboard updates. This prevents the rare case where an update could trip the licence check by reading a slightly different hardware fingerprint.
