  • Login Subtitle Uses Your Branding: The login page subtitle now uses your configured Dashboard Name from White‐Label Branding instead of the generic “LiveKit Dashboard” default.
    • 
                                
  • Background Service Restart on Resource Changes: Changing systemd memory or CPU limits from the System Resources page now restarts the affected services in the background, so the page no longer hangs on apply.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Blind Transfer Caller Cleanup: When you transfer a caller and the destination hangs up first, the caller leg is now also cleaned up automatically — no more lingering one‐sided rooms after a transfer ends. Fixes a regression where the caller would stay connected with no agent on the other end.
    • 
                                
  • Attended Transfer Polish (9 fixes): Attended (warm) transfer has been hardened with multiple fixes: hold music now plays during the consult, the audio pipeline reconnects cleanly post‐merge, post‐transfer cleanup completes properly, the consult prompt is now configurable per agent, and Redis writes during transfer are now async so they don’t block call audio.
    • 
                                
  • Blind Transfer Auto‐Hangup: In bridge‐mode blind transfer, when the caller hangs up, the destination leg is now automatically dropped instead of being left hanging.

  • Swap File UI Now Works: The Create Swap File button in System Resources no longer fails silently — the underlying swap commands have been permitted in sudoers so the UI can actually create the swap file.

  • Integrations Toggle Polish: The Show/Hide slider on Integrations no longer shifts horizontally by 8 pixels when toggled, and the failure toast now shows the correct error message instead of mismatched argument text.

  • MiniMax Test Button: The Test button next to the MiniMax API key in Settings › Integrations now correctly verifies the key against the right MiniMax endpoint (previously returned a 404).
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.22.1
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Per‐Model Pricing: Pricing is now tracked per individual model instead of per provider bucket. Each LLM, STT, and TTS model has its own rate (e.g. GPT‐4o Mini is priced separately from GPT‐4o), giving accurate cost figures on every call. Configure rates under Settings › Pricing — models are grouped by provider, with safe defaults seeded automatically for every supported model. Existing per‐provider rates remain as a fallback for any model without an explicit row.
    • 
                                
  • Per‐Model Cost Breakdown on Call Detail: The Call Details page now shows a detailed breakdown of which model was used at each stage of the call and what each one cost. Click the new blue Show Breakdown button to open a modal listing every LLM token batch, STT minute, TTS character chunk, AI summary, knowledge‐base lookup, and memory extraction with its own cost line.
    • 
                                
  • Per‐Agent Cost Attribution: Calls that were transferred or handed off between multiple agents now attribute cost to each agent separately, so multi‐agent workflows show exactly which agent contributed which spend.
    • 
                                
  • Auxiliary Costs Section: AI summary generation, mem0 memory extraction, and knowledge‐base lookups now appear as their own line items on every call — previously these were rolled into the main call cost and invisible. The call detail page has a new collapsible Auxiliary Costs section listing them.
    • 
                                
  • Speed Ratings on Every Model: The voice‐agent editor and chatbot editor now show a 1–5 star speed rating beside every LLM, STT, TTS, and Realtime model. Pick from a glance which models respond fastest in real‐world testing. Ratings come from the built‐in model validator, which exercises every provider end‐to‐end through the same SDK plugins the voice agent uses.
    • 
                                
  • Live Exchange Rates: Settings › Pricing now has a Fetch Latest Rates button that pulls current foreign‐exchange rates from frankfurter.dev with one click. Useful if you bill in a currency other than USD and want your cost figures kept up‐to‐date without manual lookups.
    • 
                                
  • Currency & Cost vs Price Split: The pricing tab now distinguishes between “cost” (what we pay the provider) and “price” (what you charge customers), with a configurable markup percentage and exchange rate. Reports display both side‐by‐side where relevant.
    • 
                                
  • Per‐Model Column in Call History: The Call History list now has a per‐model column showing exactly which model handled each call, plus a model filter so you can see only calls that used a specific model, and a cost‐sort option to rank calls by spend.
    • 
                                
  • Settings Tab Reorganisation: The General tab has been split into General and White‐Label sub‐tabs, and Time & Date now has its own sub‐tab. Currency and auxiliary cost cards have moved from General to the Pricing tab where they belong. Everything stays on familiar settings — just better organised.
    • 
                                
  • Pricing Method Column in CSV Export: The Call History CSV export now includes a Pricing Method column showing whether each call was priced per‐model or via the legacy bucket fallback. Useful when comparing old vs new pricing during a transition period.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Cleaner Call Detail Layout: The Call Details and Recording cards have been merged into a single side‐by‐side card, the cost summary draws from one source, and the Call Health panel has been repositioned for readability.
    • 
                                
  • Model Region Availability: Google Cloud Vertex AI models that aren’t available in your configured region are now greyed out with a clear note listing which regions they ARE available in (e.g. “not available in australia‐southeast1 — supported: global, us‐central1, europe‐west1”).
    • 
                                
  • Observability Drawer Defaults: The observability drawer on the call detail page now opens by default, transcription scroll padding has been doubled to keep more context visible, and every SDK span is now tagged with the call ID so spans are easy to correlate across the trace.
    • 
                                
  • Sidebar Update Pill: The “Update available” notification pill now appears inline below the Settings link in the sidebar (previously a banner across the top), keeping the chrome cleaner on small screens.
    • 
                                
  • Memory Recall Provider Mapping: Memory recall now maps dashboard provider names (e.g. “openai”, “anthropic”) to the names mem0 expects internally, fixing intermittent recall failures on chatbots that used non‐default providers.
    • 
                                
  • Star Rating Pill Styling: The “Speed rating” explanation note under each model dropdown is now styled as a spaced grey pill (white text on dark background), making it clear at a glance that the stars indicate response speed.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Update Reliability: Resolved an issue that could leave the dashboard unresponsive after applying an update. The update process now restarts the dashboard cleanly every time, so the page reloads automatically once the new version is in place.
    • 
                                
  • Google/Vertex Models No Longer Falsely Greyed Out: The agent editor incorrectly showed all Google and Vertex AI models as “requires google.generativeai SDK” even though the SDK was installed and working. The dependency check was pointing at the legacy package name; now it checks the current package and Google/Vertex models are selectable as expected.
    • 
                                
  • Health‐Check Badges for New Providers: The agent‐list Health Check badge and modal now correctly recognise OpenRouter, Groq, and Hume API keys. Previously these providers showed a red “Config Error” badge even with valid keys configured, because the health check had hardcoded lookups missing the new provider entries.
    • 
                                
  • FX Rate Button Colour: The Fetch Latest Rates button in Settings › Pricing now uses the standard blue colour for secondary actions, matching the rest of the dashboard’s button conventions.
    • 
                                
  • Realtime Region Error Messages: Picking a realtime model that isn’t available in your configured region now gives a specific, actionable error instead of a generic “construction failed” trace.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.20.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Virtual Avatars for Chatbots: Web chatbots can now show a lifelike video avatar that speaks the agent’s replies. Four providers are supported — D‐ID, Tavus, Beyond Presence, and LiveAvatar (HeyGen). Configure under the new Virtual Avatar tab on each chatbot, with controls for size, shape, position, and visibility. Test buttons are also available in Settings › Integrations.
    • 
                                
  • SMS Chatbot Delivery: Chat agents can now reach customers over SMS as well as the website widget. Twilio, Telnyx, and Tronic Cloud are supported as delivery providers. Configure under the chatbot’s SMS tab.
    • 
                                
  • Three Chatbot Modes: Each chatbot can now run in one of three modes — pure text, text + voice avatar, or full voice (visitor speaks too). Pick from the editor; the widget adapts automatically (microphone permission only requested in full‐voice mode).
    • 
                                
  • Knowledge Base for Chatbots: Chatbots can now search a knowledge base mid‐conversation, the same way voice agents already could. Attach one or more KB collections from the chatbot editor and the agent will cite facts from those documents.
    • 
                                
  • Speaker Mute in Widget: The chat widget gained a speaker icon that lets the visitor mute the agent’s audio (handy during shared screens or quiet environments). Preference persists per‐agent in the browser.
    • 
                                
  • “Save & Keep Editing”: The chatbot editor now has a Save button that keeps you on the same page instead of redirecting back to the list. Same convenience the voice‐agent editor already had.
    • 
                                
  • Unified Media Column: The Chat History list now shows a single Media column (Voice / Web / SMS) with a matching filter, replacing the previous Voice/Chat split.
    • 
                                
  • Agent‐Side Welcome: Chatbot welcome messages now come from the agent itself when the session starts, matching how voice agents greet callers (consistent timing, captured in transcripts, persisted to chat history).
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Chatbot Reliability Rebuilt: Mid‐conversation disconnects on knowledge‐base questions are gone. Text chatbots now use the LiveKit‐recommended text‐stream channel instead of the lower‐level data channel that occasionally hung after heavy turns. Replies and visitor messages flow through a reliable, ordered stream that doesn’t go silent under load.
    • 
                                
  • Returning‐Visitor Memory: Memory recall now works for text chatbots, not just voice. A returning visitor with stored memories is recognised on session start (name, phone, preferences, prior bookings …) so the chatbot doesn’t have to ask again.
    • 
                                
  • Stale‐Room Recovery: When the agent service restarts (after an update, for example), in‐flight chatbot sessions no longer go silent. The worker scans for orphaned chat rooms on startup and silently re‐dispatches itself into them. The visitor’s next message just gets answered normally.
    • 
                                
  • Avatar Disconnect Handling: If the avatar provider drops mid‐call, the widget now hides the video element cleanly and the chat continues without lip‐sync rather than freezing.
    • 
                                
  • Single‐Page Chat‐History Detail: The chat detail page now shows all info (IDs, LLM, cost, metrics, conversation, summary, analysis) on one scrollable page instead of switching between Overview and Conversation tabs.
    • 
                                
  • Timezone Picker UTC Offsets: Every entry in Settings › General › Timezone now shows its UTC offset, e.g. “Australia/Perth (AWST, UTC+8)”, “UAE / Dubai — Asia/Dubai (GST, UTC+4)”, “America/New_York (EST/EDT, UTC−5)”.
    • 
                                
  • STT/TTS Dropdown Sync: The Speech Recognition and Voice tabs in the chatbot editor now mirror the voice‐agent editor exactly, so the same providers and models are offered everywhere.
    • 
                                
  • Better Voice/Web Classification: Chat history now distinguishes a voice call from a web‐widget session using visitor‐side signals, eliminating the “voice agent on web” misclassification.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Chat‐History LLM/Metrics Card: The LLM provider box and Metrics card now render correctly for chatbot sessions (previously showed “‐” because the lookup only checked voice‐agent storage).
    • 
                                
  • Widget History Order: The widget’s history poll was reading the oldest 100 messages instead of the newest 100, hiding recent replies from returning visitors. Now correctly returns the most recent messages.
    • 
                                
  • Mem0 Config Propagation: Chatbots with memory enabled now actually save memories on session end (the configuration flag was being dropped at agent startup).
    • 
                                
  • Inactivity Timeout Reset: Returning visitors no longer get instantly disconnected because of a stale activity timestamp from a prior session.
    • 
                                
  • SMS Tronic Cloud Auth: The Tronic Cloud SMS provider now sends the API key correctly via the documented query parameter (previously used a header that wasn’t accepted).
    • 
                                
  • Avatar Audio Routing: Text‐input replies on voice‐with‐avatar chatbots now correctly route through TTS so the avatar actually speaks (was silent on text replies).
    • 
                                
  • LiveAvatar Concurrency Errors: Concurrency‐limit failures from LiveAvatar are now surfaced clearly in the widget rather than appearing as a generic startup failure.
    • 
                                
  • Editor Tooltip Hints: The little (?) info circles on the chatbot editor now actually show their tooltip text on hover (Bootstrap was missing its initialisation step).
    • 
                                
  • Settings Resources Display: The System tab now shows the configured memory cap rather than the failsafe MemoryMax, and the “Used” badge has readable contrast.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.19.4
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Smart Resource Suggestions: The System tab on the Settings page now shows recommended memory caps for every service (agent worker, LiveKit, Egress, Qdrant, Redis, Dashboard, SIP), sized automatically for your server’s RAM and CPU. Bigger servers get bigger suggestions; small servers get safe ones. Click “Apply” on any row to use the suggested cap — the service restarts briefly. The reading is plain English: “sized for your server (X GB RAM, Y CPU), assume up to N calls at once, with/without recording, and a tiny/small/medium/large Knowledge Base.”
    • 
                                
  • “Use My IP” on Whitelisted IPs: The Security tab now has a “Use My IP” button beside the Add‐to‐Whitelist form. Click it, your current IP fills in automatically, then type a label (“Office”, “Home laptop”) and click the green plus. Same one‐click affordance the MCP API key form already had.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Bigger Timezone Dropdown: The General tab’s timezone picker now offers around 60 entries across Australia, Asia, Europe, Americas, Africa (new), and Pacific. Country names appear at the start of the label so typing “India”, “Brazil”, “Spain”, “Philippines”, etc. jumps straight to the right entry. Australia entries are unchanged. Existing saved timezones still work — only the visible labels were updated.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • UTC Now Saves Cleanly: Selecting “UTC” from the timezone dropdown previously returned “Invalid timezone format” and refused to save. The validator has been replaced with the standard Python timezone library, so UTC and every other valid IANA timezone now save without complaint.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.19.3
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • OpenAI GPT Realtime 2 Support: The new GPT‐5‐class realtime voice model from OpenAI is now selectable in the agent editor under Pipeline Mode › Realtime › OpenAI. It’s the most capable OpenAI realtime model to date, with stronger reasoning, better recovery on interruptions, and improved natural speech. Pick “GPT Realtime 2 (Latest, GPT‐5‐class)” from the model dropdown to use it. The default voice “Marin” remains in place.
    • 
                                
  • Per‐Model Pricing for GPT Realtime 2: A dedicated pricing entry “OpenAI Realtime — gpt‐realtime‐2” has been added under Settings › Pricing › Realtime. This lets you rate this premium model independently of the rest of the OpenAI realtime line. Seeded with default rates — adjust to match OpenAI’s confirmed published rate when available.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.19.2
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Captured Data in After‐Call Reports: The “AI Conversation Analysis” report now includes every field you’ve set up under an agent’s “Data Extraction Fields” tab. For email reports, drop {{extracted_data_html}} into your template and a tidy block of captured fields appears in the email. For webhook reports, tick the new extracted_data field and the webhook payload includes a structured object with every captured value — ready to feed into n8n, Zapier, your CRM, or any other automation.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Helpful Tip on the Post‐Call Summary Editor: When configuring a Post‐Call Summary report, an info note now points to the AI Conversation Analysis report type if you need the agent’s captured data fields included.
    • 
                                
  • Silence Re‐engagement Mode is Now Settable via the Dashboard API: External tools (such as Claude Code) connecting to the dashboard via the built‐in API can now change which prompt the agent uses to re‐engage a silent caller (“Are you still there?”, repeat last response, or AI‐generated). Previously this dropdown could only be changed in the dashboard UI.
    • 
                                
  • User Away Timeout Slider Capped at 60 Seconds: The agent editor’s “Silence before agent re‐engages” slider now tops out at 60 seconds (was 120). 60s is already long for a real conversation; the lower max prevents accidental misconfiguration.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Max Call Duration API Documentation Fix: The dashboard’s built‐in API documentation for “Max Call Duration” previously stated the value was in seconds when it is actually in minutes (matching the editor label). External tools following the old documentation could have configured a 10‐hour cap thinking it was 10 minutes. Documentation is now correct in all places.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.19.1
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Agent Failed to Answer Calls When a Webhook Tool Had Optional Fields Before Required Ones: Voice agents could ring forever and never answer if any webhook tool’s parameter list had an optional field listed before a required one. The agent process now reorders parameters internally before starting, so any field order configured in the dashboard works reliably.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Inline Search on the AI Agents Page: The AI Agents list page gains a search box rendered inline with the page heading so you can filter agents without scrolling.
    • 
                                
  • Search Bars on Tools Tabs: Each Tools tab (Built‐in, Webhook, MCP) now has its own search bar to quickly find a tool by name.
    • 
                                
  • Vivid Outbound Badge on SIP Numbers: The Outbound badge on the Telephony Numbers page is now a more visible orange so the difference between Inbound and Outbound numbers stands out at a glance.
    • 
                                
  • 3CX Setup Guide — Firewall Ports Step: The downloadable “Connecting Dashboard to 3CX via SIP URI” guide gains a new “Step 0 — Open the firewall ports” section listing the exact ports that need to be open and a reminder about 3CX’s separate Anti‐Hacking whitelist layer.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.19.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Smart Silence Re‐Engagement: When the agent and caller both fall silent, the agent now speaks first instead of waiting indefinitely. New per‐agent controls in Behaviour → Conversation Dynamics: a configurable silence timer (5–120 s, 1‐second granularity), an enable/disable toggle, max attempts before hanging up, and three actions to choose from — ask “Are you still there?”, repeat the last response, or let the AI generate a context‐aware re‐engagement based on the conversation. Works in both Standard and Realtime pipelines.
    • 
                                
  • SIP Setup Wizard: A new step‐by‐step wizard walks operators through creating SIP trunks for seven supported providers (Twilio, Telnyx, Tronic Cloud, 3CX, Vonage, Plivo, Generic). Includes pre‐filled allowed‐IP defaults, agent + time‐profile pickers on the dispatch rule step, an auto‐record toggle, and operator‐named trunks. Provider‐specific walkthroughs are linked from the wizard.
    • 
                                
  • 3CX Integration Guides: Two new guides under Settings → Notes/Guides → Guides — “Connecting Dashboard to 3CX via SIP URI” (full bidirectional voice setup) and “Connecting 3CX SMS Chat” (provider‐agnostic Generic SMS setup). Each guide is downloadable, with screenshots and exact field values for the 3CX wizard.
    • 
                                
  • Per‐Call Caller‐ID on PBX Transfers: When the AI transfers an inbound caller to a 3CX extension, the destination phone now shows the original caller’s number by default — not a static value — so the 3CX user can see who’s actually calling and call back. Operators can lock this to a fixed value (e.g. a main DID or “AIReceptionist”) by entering a value in the PBX trunk’s Caller‐ID extension field. Includes a Diversion header on every transfer for accurate 3CX CDR records.
    • 
                                
  • Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7: Added to the AI Summary and Enrich‐with‐AI provider list as a thinking model. Use it for deep‐reasoning tasks like generating call summaries or enhancing system prompts. Sonnet 4.6 stays the default for both. Opus 4.7 is intentionally not added to the voice agent dropdown — thinking models are too slow for real‐time conversation.
    • 
                                
  • Settings Tab Reorganisation: Long settings tabs are now split into focused sub‐tabs — Pricing (General + Provider Pricing → LLM/STT/TTS/Realtime), Email (Configuration / Notifications & Alerts / Templates / Log), Storage (Backup + Storage), System (System Resources + System Logs), and Notes/Guides (Notes + Guides). Card‐grid Guides display with hover lift, big tap‐targets, and matching styling across all parent tabs.
    • 
                                
  • Unified SIP Trunks Page: Inbound and Outbound trunks now share one tabbed page in Telephony. Outbound trunks gain a Type column with PBX/PSTN coloured badges so it’s immediately clear which trunk does what.
    • 
                                
  • Tools Page Split into Tabs: The Tools page now organises Built‐in Tools, Webhook Tools, and MCP Servers into separate tabs for cleaner navigation.
    • 
                                
  • One‐Click Test‐Dial: Each transfer destination on the Blind Transfer / Attended Transfer tools gains a one‐click test‐dial button so operators can verify routing before going live.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Plain‐English Silence Controls: The silence‐related controls in the agent editor have been renamed (“Silence before agent re‐engages”, “Re‐engage caller on silence”, “Max re‐engagement attempts before hanging up”) and physically grouped next to End Call on Silence so the two related features stop getting confused. New default values match industry norms (10 s timer, 2 attempts).
    • 
                                
  • Faster Agent Response Loop: Background telemetry that previously did Redis writes on the agent’s response loop has been moved off‐loop entirely — agent responses now feel snappier on metric‐heavy turns and on tool calls with large outputs. No visible behaviour change, just less mid‐turn lag.
    • 
                                
  • System Resources Sub‐Tab Loading: Fixed a regression where the System Resources panel under Settings → System never finished its “Loading…” spinner after the parent tab restructure. Legacy ?tab=resources URLs continue to work.
    • 
                                
  • Setup Wizard Polish: Wizard name field is now mandatory and entered manually (no auto‐suggest); persistent error/note alerts no longer auto‐dismiss; agent + time‐profile pickers added to the dispatch rule step; Tronic Cloud portal link points to the correct URL; redundant “Manage” link removed from the Time Profile picker.
    • 
                                
  • Caller‐ID Field Clarity: The PBX trunk “Caller‐ID extension (optional)” field now has a persistent info box with a live preview showing exactly what blank vs filled does, so operators can see the outcome before saving.
    • 
                                
  • Compact Notes‐Tab Guides: SIP provider setup guides on the Notes/Guides tab are now displayed as a card grid with icons, descriptions, and download arrows that fade in on hover (Stripe/Vercel pattern).
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Dispatch Rule Delete Buttons: Delete buttons on the SIP Trunks Dispatch Rules page were silently dead because of a Jinja escaping issue in the inline onclick attribute. Now use safe data‐* attributes and work reliably.
    • 
                                
  • Trunk Edit Modal: When a PBX trunk is in “auto” caller‐ID mode (blank field), the edit modal now correctly shows the field as blank rather than leaking the auto‐derived placeholder value.
    • 
                                
  • User Management Tab: User Management content no longer disappears after the System parent tab merge.
    • 
                                
  • Webhook Tools Tab: Webhook Tools tab no longer renders empty after the MCP collapse removal — tag balance fixed.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.18.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Agent Observability: The Conversation tab on every call detail page now includes an interactive audio waveform, a 5-lane event timeline (User / LLM / TTS / Tool / System), and a side drawer with Details, Logs, and Trace tabs. Click any timeline marker or transcript line to seek the recording to that moment; press space to play / pause; the matching transcript line highlights and auto-scrolls in sync with the playhead.
    • 
                                
  • Observability Storage Backend: A new “Observability Storage” panel in Settings → Storage lets you choose Local, S3, or GCS for archived per-call observability data — mirroring the existing Recording and Call History storage choices. Includes a “Browse bucket” helper, a skip-local-fallback toggle, and a pending-upload retry button.
    • 
                                
  • Storage At-a-Glance Badges: The top of the Storage tab now shows six count cards — Local and Cloud counts for Recordings, Call History, and Observability — so you can see exactly where your data lives without drilling into each panel.
    • 
                                
  • Bulk Pre-Known Caller Memories: The Agent Memory tab gains a bulk-upload card — paste or import a list of facts about a caller (CSV/JSON) ahead of their first call so the agent already knows them. Each fact can be marked persistent so it survives memory pruning.
    • 
                                
  • Brain Icon & Memory Badges on Knowledge Base Page: The Knowledge Base page now uses a brain icon and shows Memory-vs-KB badges so it’s clear at a glance which content type each row represents.
    • 
                                
  • MCP Tools for Observability: External tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) can now query per-call observability via two new MCP tools — get_call_observability(call_id, since_ms, limit, lane, kind, errors_only) and list_calls_with_observability(limit, offset) — with pagination, gzip on large responses, and rate limiting to protect the server.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Recording Playback Modal Removed: The pop-up audio modal on the call detail page has been retired in favour of the embedded waveform on the Conversation tab. The Overview tab keeps a Download button for calls with recordings.
    • 
                                
  • Faster MP4 Playback in the Browser: Recordings are now post-processed at egress so the browser can start streaming them immediately, rather than downloading the whole file before audio begins.
    • 
                                
  • Stable Hangup & Tool Preface Audio: Goodbye phrases now play fully before the call disconnects, and tool prefaces play before the tool fires — no more cut-off or out-of-order phrases.
    • 
                                
  • Cleaner Eager EOT Slider: The Eager End-of-Turn slider in the agent editor is capped at a safe upper bound and is automatically clamped against the EOT threshold at runtime so users can’t accidentally configure a value that prevents turn-taking.
    • 
                                
  • Knowledge Base Stats Layout: Knowledge Base & Memory stats are merged into a single tidy row matching the Reports page layout.
    • 
                                
  • Settings → Storage Compaction: The Cloud Sync row has been compressed to match the rest of the Storage page; redundant inline badges replaced by the new at-a-glance count cards.
    • 
                                
  • Settings → Dependencies: OpenTelemetry is now listed in the Dependencies tab and updated automatically when the dashboard self-updates.
    • 
                                
  • Faster Dashboard Startup: A startup-time check that occasionally hung for the full SIP timeout has been capped, so the dashboard never blocks on a slow first migration call.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Mid-Call Lag Eliminated: A telemetry path was previously doing work on the agent’s response loop and could cause noticeable mid-call silence. All telemetry work has been moved to a background thread — calls now feel as responsive with observability on as off.
    • 
                                
  • Conversation Tab Layout: Several long-tail layout bugs fixed — the observability section no longer collapses to its header, the transcript is no longer truncated behind a height cap, and the side drawer no longer pushes the transcript off-screen.
    • 
                                
  • Transcript Highlight Now Tracks the Audio: The transcript line that highlights as the recording plays is now tied to the actual audio start of each turn rather than the SDK’s event timestamp, so the visible highlight matches what you hear (previously up to 11 seconds late on long answers).
    • 
                                
  • Mid-Sentence Audio Cutouts on Flux STT Agents: Fixed a case where Deepgram Flux STT could cut the agent off mid-sentence on certain turn-taking patterns.
    • 
                                
  • Settings Page Save: Saving the Storage settings tab no longer produces a blank page when the new observability storage panel is configured.
    • 
                                
  • Memory Bulk-Upload Edge Cases: Bulk-upload flow now handles malformed rows, duplicates, and the persistent flag correctly per audit feedback.
    • 
                                
  • Hangup Tool Disconnects Reliably: The hangup tool now disconnects the SIP caller right after the goodbye phrase — no more lingering empty rooms.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.17.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Reseller Account Type: A new account type sits between sub-user and admin — resellers can create their own sub-users (and assign agents to them) within configurable per-resource caps you set when creating the reseller. Slots are freed automatically when sub-users or agents are deleted, and your existing power-user accounts keep their full access.
    • 
                                
  • Knowledge Base & Memory Tabs: The Knowledge Base page is now split into two clearly labelled tabs — “Knowledge Base” and “Agent Memory” — so you can switch between long-term knowledge and conversation memory without scrolling through one combined view.
    • 
                                
  • Configurable Warm-Idle Agent Processes: The “Keep Agent Worker Warm” setting in Settings → System has been upgraded from on/off to a numeric selector (0, 1, or 2 processes). Setting 2 lets back-to-back calls start instantly without waiting for a process to warm up.
    • 
                                
  • xAI Region Selector: New region dropdown in Settings → Integrations for xAI — pick US-East or US-West to route Grok traffic to the closest endpoint for lower latency.
    • 
                                
  • xAI Grok 4.20 Models: Added Grok 4.20 Reasoning and Grok 4.20 (Speed, non-reasoning) to the LLM dropdown for voice agents, web chat, AI summaries, and the API tester.
    • 
                                
  • xAI Grok Voice Think Fast 1.0: Added as the default realtime model for xAI agents (replaces the older non-reasoning model), tagged as “(Latest)” in the dropdown.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Faster First-Call Response: The voice activity detection model is now loaded once at worker startup rather than on the first call — so the very first call after a restart no longer pays the warm-up cost.
    • 
                                
  • Migration to Current Google AI Library: AI call summaries using Google AI Studio now use the supported google-genai package; the deprecated google-generativeai package has been removed. Error logs are no longer flooded with deprecation warnings.
    • 
                                
  • Reduced Log Noise: Recurring startup warnings about optional dependencies have been demoted to debug level so the agent log focuses on real issues.
    • 
                                
  • Cleaner Grok Model Labels: Removed the rotation-prone “(Newest)” / “(Instant)” suffixes; newest models simply appear first in the dropdown.
    • 
                                
  • Cleaner Agent Memory Headings: Removed the “(mem0)” technical reference from Agent Memory headings — the page now reads as plain “Agent Memory”.
    • 
                                
  • Tightened Sub-User Permission UI: Sub-user permission controls are now consistent across the user editor — clearer labelling and matching toggle behaviour.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Preemptive Generation Setting Now Applies: Fixed a bug where the “Preemptive Generation” toggle in the agent editor had no effect — agents with this setting enabled now correctly start generating responses while the user is still speaking.
    • 
                                
  • AWS Bedrock Tool Conversation Reliability: Fixed a silent error that could cause agents to stop responding mid-call after using a tool (for example DTMF collection).
    • 
                                
  • Smoother Turn-Taking with Flux STT: When using Deepgram Flux turn detection with a low silence threshold, the threshold is now automatically raised to a safe minimum to prevent agents from cutting off users too early.
    • 
                                
  • Cleaner Shutdown for Post-Call Summaries: Long-running summaries no longer block the agent worker from shutting down cleanly; truncated summaries are now retried automatically rather than lost.
    • 
                                
  • Misrouted-Call Handling: Calls arriving with no agent configuration attached now shut down cleanly rather than leaving the job in an ambiguous state.
    • 
                                
  • Agent Tester Sub-User Dropdown: Fixed a case where the Agent Tester user dropdown was empty for sub-users with assigned agents — the dropdown now populates correctly.
    • 
                                
  • Reseller Cap Enforcement: Closed several edge cases where reseller resource caps could be bypassed; deletes now reliably free a slot back to the cap budget.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.16.4
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Maintenance Release: A small maintenance update with internal housekeeping improvements. No new features or settings changes in this release.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.16.3
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • 3CX Messaging Tool: New built-in tool that lets voice AI agents send SMS messages directly into your 3CX phone system during a call. Configure a 3CX Generic SMS webhook URL, then set up a list of named recipients (e.g. “Sales”, “Support”) and sender identities — the agent picks by name. Settings work system-wide or per-agent, just like the other tools. Ideal for notifying a 3CX user about a caller, handing off context to a queue, or logging details mid-call.
    • 
                                
  • Send Test Message Button: The 3CX Messaging tool configuration modal has a new “Send Test Message” panel — pick a recipient and sender from the saved list, type a message, and fire a real test through your 3CX webhook without needing a live call to verify your setup.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Expanded MCP Tool Management: The built-in MCP server now exposes every tool's configuration — external MCP clients (like Claude Code) can read the schema of any built-in tool, view or change its global defaults, set per-agent overrides, and trigger the “Send Test Message” action remotely. Covers every existing tool, not just 3CX Messaging.
    • 
                                
  • Smart Phone Number Handling (3CX): The 3CX Messaging tool accepts numbers in Australian national format (0412000001), international dial format (0061412000001), full E.164 (+61412000001), or with spaces and punctuation — and normalises them correctly in every case, with a clear error for malformed input.
    • 
                                
  • Security Improvements: Additional validation has been added around the 3CX Messaging tool's webhook address.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.16.2
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Update All Button: Settings → Integrations → Dependencies now has an “Update All” button at the top of the Available Updates card. One click rolls through every pending package update, two at a time, with a live “N of M done” counter. Failed rows stay highlighted so you can retry just those.
    • 
                                
  • Click-to-Copy Phone Numbers: Each number in Telephony → Numbers is now clickable — one tap copies the full number to your clipboard with a green tick confirmation. Manual drag-select and Ctrl+C still work.
    • 
                                
  • Agent Tester Provider + Model Picker: The text-mode Agent Tester now uses a two-step dropdown (Provider first, then Model) — the same pattern as the voice agent editor. Much easier to navigate.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • LiveKit Agents 1.5.6 Compatible: The LiveKit Agents stack and every plugin have been upgraded to the latest 1.5.6 release line. The Dependencies tab Upgrade button now succeeds on existing installs without manual intervention.
    • 
                                
  • Smarter LiveKit Agents Upgrade: The “Upgrade LiveKit Agents” button now automatically reconciles conflicting dependency versions before running the upgrade — so a new release that requires a specific library version no longer fails with a cryptic “version solving failed” error. A backup of the dependency file is taken before any rewrite and restored automatically if anything goes wrong.
    • 
                                
  • Service-Down Alerts in Your Timezone: Service-down notifications now show timestamps in the timezone configured in Settings, instead of UTC.
    • 
                                
  • New Alert-Check Intervals: Added 10-minute and 15-minute options to the service alert-check interval dropdown, and removed the overly aggressive 30-second option.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Agent Tester Text Mode: Fixed text-mode testing being broken; it now works end-to-end and shows the exact same LLM list as the voice agent editor.
    • 
                                
  • Attended Transfer — Hold-Music Trap: Fixed a case where the supervisor's destination could silently fail to answer but the call was still marked as successfully transferred, leaving the caller stuck on hold music. The tool now reliably detects a missing supervisor, rolls the transfer back, and returns the caller to the agent.
    • 
                                
  • Attended Transfer — Silence Monitor: The silence monitor is now paused before the supervisor dial begins, so it can no longer fire during the dial window.
    • 
                                
  • Attended Transfer — Consultation Timeout: The “consultation timeout” setting now actually enforces a timeout — previously it was documented but never wired to a timer. Default is 120 seconds.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.16.1
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • New OpenAI Models: Added GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 Mini, GPT-5.4 Nano and GPT-5 Nano to both the voice agent and web chat LLM dropdowns. Previous “GPT-5.4 Instant” entries never existed at OpenAI and have been removed.
    • 
                                
  • Updated OpenAI Realtime Models: Added GPT Realtime 1.5 and GPT Realtime Mini, and replaced GPT-4o Realtime Preview / GPT-4o Mini Realtime Preview ahead of their OpenAI shutdown on 7 May 2026. Existing agents still using the old realtime models are automatically remapped to the new ones at runtime, so nothing breaks.
    • 
                                
  • AWS Bedrock Service Tier: New dropdown under Settings → Integrations lets you pick Standard, Priority, or Flex tiers for Bedrock calls — useful for balancing cost against latency.
    • 
                                
  • Claude Haiku 3.5 on Bedrock: Added Claude Haiku 3.5 (including a US latency-optimised variant) to the Bedrock model list for voice and web chat agents.
    • 
                                
  • Bedrock Region Selector: New region dropdown for AWS Bedrock so you can control where calls are routed for data-residency or latency reasons.
    • 
                                
  • Amazon Nova Lite & Nova 2 Lite: Added two new Amazon Nova models to the Bedrock dropdown.
    • 
                                
  • Web Chat ↔ Voice Agent Model Parity: The web chat editor now shows the exact same LLM dropdown as the voice agent editor, so you're no longer locked out of models on one side.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Extended Reasoning Moved to Web Chat: The extended-reasoning toggle now lives in the web chat editor (where latency isn't critical) rather than the voice agent editor.
    • 
                                
  • No More Unsaved-Changes Popup: The web chat editor no longer shows the “Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved” warning when you click away.
    • 
                                
  • Cleaner Bedrock Model List: Removed several APAC Sonnet 4.5/4.6 entries that weren't actually available on AWS.
    • 
                            

                            
 Bug Fixes

                            
    
                                
  • Voice Agent Reasoning Text Loss: Fixed a bug where re-saving a voice agent would wipe the reasoning-mode text field.
    • 
                                
  • Call History Race Condition: Fixed a rare race where two calls ending at the same moment could corrupt the daily call bundle in Redis.
    • 
                                
  • Call Completion Reliability: Call records are now always finalised via a shutdown callback, so the call timeline won't show incomplete entries if the worker is restarted mid-call.
    • 
                                
  • Web Chat Bedrock Text Routing: Fixed Bedrock models not being routed correctly in text-only web chat mode.
    • 
                                
  • Bedrock Extended Thinking: Claude 3.5 and older 3.x models no longer receive the “thinking” instruction block they don't support.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.16.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Web Chat Daily Limits: Every chat agent now has a “Max sessions per day” setting in its editor. When the limit is reached, the widget politely refuses new visitors until midnight (UTC) and resumes automatically. Protects you from surprise AI costs if a malicious visitor (or a runaway script on your own site) tries to hammer your chat widget.
    • 
                                
  • Per-Visitor Daily Cap: Global setting under Settings → Security stops any single visitor (identified by IP) from starting more than N widget sessions per day across all your agents. Default is 20 per visitor per day.
    • 
                                
  • Usage Badges on the Chat Agents List: Each chat agent now shows a colour-coded badge — green while under 80% of today's limit, amber at 80% and above, red “Paused” when the daily limit is reached.
    • 
                                
  • Limit-Reached Email Alert: New report type “Widget Abuse — Daily Limit Reached” can be added under Reports to email you when a chat agent hits its daily limit. Uses a new branded system email template that matches your existing white-label styling. Fires at most once per agent per day.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Safe On Update Day: Existing chat agents inherit “no limit” on upgrade so nobody's high-traffic widget gets silently paused. The 50-sessions/day default only applies to chat agents you create from this version onwards. Change the limit any time in the agent editor — raising it resumes the widget immediately.
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.15.1
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • White-Label Now Applies Everywhere: System emails (password reset, test email, reports, notifications) and pre-login pages (Login, Forgot Password, Reset Password, Two-Factor Authentication, Logout, License Activation) now use your Dashboard Name and footer settings from Settings → Branding. Previously these still showed the default product name even after white-labeling.
    • 
                                
  • Cleaner Fresh-Install Defaults: Fresh installs no longer default the footer link to an external URL — the footer shows the Dashboard Name and year until you configure your own URL and text under Settings → Footer.
    • 
                                
  • Email Header vs Sender Separated: The “From” name shown in your recipient's inbox stays controlled by Settings → Email (From Name), while the email's visible header and footer now read from your Dashboard Name — so the two can be different if you want (e.g. sender “Support Team” + brand “Acme Voice AI”).
    • 
                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                v1.15.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • External REST API for Outbound Calls: New Bearer-authenticated REST API so workflow tools like n8n, Zapier, Make, and custom scripts can trigger outbound calls. Generate a key under Settings → Integrations → REST API, paste it into your workflow tool's HTTP Request node, and fire calls with a small JSON body (agent, number, optional per-call variables).
    • 
                                
  • Dynamic Variables at Call Time: Pass caller name, company, custom fields, etc. in the API request and the agent substitutes them into the system prompt, greeting, and voicemail message using {{placeholder}}-style tags — so each call can be personalised without editing the agent.
    • 
                                
  • Call Status Lookup: Second endpoint (GET /external/v1/calls/{id}) so workflows can poll whether a call is still active, has ended, or never connected — scoped per-key so each key only sees its own calls.
    • 
                                
  • Flexible Trunk Selection: Pass either an explicit SIP trunk ID or just the caller-ID number — the dashboard auto-picks the right trunk when possible. Ambiguous numbers surface a clear error.
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Settings → Integrations Page Restructure: Three clear sub-tabs — "API Keys" for provider keys (OpenAI, Deepgram, etc., unchanged), new "REST API" for workflow tool keys, and "MCP Server" (renamed from the confusing "Integrations") for Claude Code / Cursor keys.
    • 
                                
  • Safeguards For External Keys: New REST API keys default to 10 requests/minute (tighter than MCP's 60 because each call costs phone minutes), request bodies are size-capped, and dynamic variables have per-value limits so a leaked key or misconfigured workflow can't exhaust your trunk minutes or the agent worker.
    • 
                                
  • Optional Retry Protection: The REST API supports an Idempotency-Key header so workflow tools that auto-retry on transient failures won't double-dial the same contact within 24 hours.
    •

 Bug Fixes

The region picker now clearly separates regions that work for Chirp 3 HD from regions that work for Gemini voices, and warns when the two are confused.
    •

Virginia, Columbus, Dallas, Oregon, Las Vegas) and four more EU regions (Warsaw, Finland, Madrid, Belgium, Netherlands). Previously the picker only offered us and eu multi-region aliases, which Gemini voices don't accept.

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Per-Agent Conversational Memory: Agents can now remember facts about callers across calls — things like their name, preferences, past issues, and follow-ups they were waiting on. Memories are stored per agent and automatically surfaced at the start of each call so conversations feel continuous. Configure under the new Knowledge Base / Memory page
    • 
                                
  • Memory Configuration Controls: Per-agent score threshold, custom extraction prompt, configurable embedding provider, and limits for how many memories are kept per caller and per session. Sensible defaults (50 total / 10 per caller / 10 per session) are applied out of the box, with FIFO pruning to keep the most relevant entries
    •

    •

    •

    •

  • Sidebar Navigation: "Knowledge Base" renamed to "Knowledge Base / Memory" to reflect the new memory feature

    • 
                                
  • Non-Blocking Memory Pre-Load: Memory pre-load at call start no longer blocks the agent's greeting, so callers hear the greeting immediately even while memories are being loaded in the background
    • 
                                
  • Extraction Prompt Auto-Fill: Data Extraction Fields are automatically appended to the memory extraction prompt, and the default prompt is populated for new agents so memory works correctly out of the box
    •

    •

 Bug Fixes

    • 
                                
  • Faster Manual Retry: "Check provider now" button wait time between clicks reduced from 30 seconds to 10 seconds
    • 
                                
  • Live Auto-Refresh: The provider health popup now refreshes automatically every 15 seconds while open, so fresh probe results appear without needing to close and re-open
    • 
                                
  • Chart Sizing: The 24-hour response-time chart in the Details popup is no longer oversized — it now fits neatly inside the popup regardless of how many data points are plotted
    •

                                v1.13.0
                            

                            
 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • LLM Auto-Failover with Health Monitoring: Each agent can now be configured with a primary LLM and up to two backups. Periodic background health probes automatically route new calls to a healthy backup if the primary is degraded, and switch back once it recovers — keeping voice agents responsive even when a provider or region has issues. Configure under the LLM tab in the agent editor
    • 
                                
  • Extended Reasoning for AWS Bedrock Claude: Per-agent extended reasoning mode for AWS Bedrock Anthropic Claude models, with separate switches for voice calls and web chat. When enabled, the agent may pause to think before replying — more considered answers at the cost of speed. Newer Claude models decide per-message whether to think; older Claude models always add a short reasoning step. Disabled by default. Enabling for voice calls adds noticeable silence before replies and is not recommended for most agents
    • 
                            

                            
 Improvements

                            
    
                                
  • Agent Editor Tooltips: Clearer help text across the LLM tab explaining the latency / cost / quality trade-offs of fallback, caching, and reasoning options
    • 
                                
  • MCP Field Coverage: External API clients (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) can now read and write the new fallback and reasoning fields via the agent configuration API
    •

 New Features

                            
    
                                
  • Agent Latency Pack: Three opt-in speed wins — Anthropic / Bedrock Claude prompt caching (cuts cost and time-to-first-token on stable prompts), Flux endpointing delay fix (Response Delay no longer stacks on top of Flux's own wait), and Agent Warm Idle worker (first call of the day 2-5s faster; toggle in Settings → System for constrained hardware)
    • 
                                
  • MCP Prompt Audit Trail: When an external tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, or scripts) edits an agent's prompt via the API, a prompt-history entry is automatically created — tagged with the API key name — so browser edits and programmatic edits share the same Versions tab, diffs, and one-click rollback
    • 
                                
  • MCP Full Agent Coverage: External API clients can now read and write every agent configuration field, including realtime audio-to-audio models, voicemail / IVR detection, LLM fallback chain, ElevenLabs / Hume voice fine-tuning, Azure deployment names, knowledge-base assignments, folder placement, and all conversation dynamics — previously limited to a small subset
    •

  • Agent Help Refresh: Agent editor Help modal now covers prompt versioning source labels, MCP / API access setup, and links to the full field reference
    • 
                                
  • MCP Schema Discovery: get_agent_config_reference() returns the complete list of writable fields, enums, nested-dict keys, and merge semantics — so MCP clients can self-discover the full schema without trial and error

 New Features
